quotes.quote: Onlymammycanloveme is a fine, big horse. He has a real stamp of a chaser and hopefully that's what he'll go on to do. I think the further in trip he goes the better - Seamus Neville, trainer.

runners.comment: Dual course winner, drop to 2m against him latest, chance stepped back up in trip
runners.spotlight: Won on handicap debut here (2m, heavy) in November; won again off his revised mark of 120 here in January (2m5f, sft-hvy); drop back to 2m didn't suit at Fairyhouse latest; better expected over this longer trip; chance.

quotes.race: Albert Bartlett Triple Crown Series Qualifier Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Powerful never travelled in Leopardstown, and he lugged to the right so maybe he's happier going right-handed than left-handed. He's a big horse to organise and he probably learned a lot in Leopardstown as everything happened quick there over two miles. He loved it today over two and a half. He'll probably come back here for the final and we'll see where we go in between, I'll talk to Frank [Berry] and we'll see. He'll be a lovely chaser for next year. He was a very weak horse but has got a lot stronger - Jessica Harrington, trainer.

runners.comment: 3-5 over hurdles, still going okay when brought down on latest, could go well
runners.spotlight: British raider is 3-5 over hurdles; won his maiden at Musselburgh (2m4f, gd-sft) and then added handicaps at Haydock (2m5f, gd-sft) and Kelso (22.5f, heavy); brought down four out when still going okay at Kelso latest; could go well.

stable_tour.quote: He's been a star. He seems to be improving all the time, he's very versatile and appears to go on any ground. He's qualified for the Cab On Target final at Kelso on Saturday week, which is a valuable race for a horse with his rating. He's also qualified for the Triple Crown final at Punchestown, so if he runs well at Kelso he could go there as well. 13-03-26

runners.comment: Dual purpose, up 11lb for Naas win in January, Gowran Flat win latest, player
runners.spotlight: Dual-purpose; has won three of his last four, two over hurdles and on the Flat at Gowran on latest; raised 11lb for his latest win over timber at Naas (18.5f, heavy) in January; this is harder but he did that easily and he is ground versatile; player.

quotes.race: Albert Bartlett Triple Crown Series At Punchestown Festival 2026 Qualifier Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Matt Connor had run well at Leopardstown and we thought the extra two furlongs would be no burden to him. He's a very small horse so Luke said he might be better riding him out wider and away from other horses the last day, so Keith did the same today. He jumped great, handled the ground well. I don't know how strong the race was but it looked alright on paper. He might give the owners a day out in the Coral Cup or something. He'll get a fair hike for that. The final of this race at Punchestown is also worth considering as it's a 100,000euros race - Philip Dempsey, trainer.

runners.comment: 2-2 since tackling handicaps, up 7lb for 2.25l win latest, unexposed and progressive
runners.spotlight: British raider has won his first two starts in handicap company, by a neck at Wetherby (21.5f, soft) and by 2.25l over the same C&D on good ground off 4lb higher; has gone up another 7lb but he's unexposed and looks progressive.

runners.comment: No win since October 2024, well beaten all four starts this season, others preferred
runners.spotlight: Has come up dry since winning a handicap chase at Galway in October 2024; soundly beaten all four starts this term; won his maiden hurdle here but others arrive in better form.

quotes.race: Marlin Hotel Dublin, Supporting The National Breast Cancer Research Institute Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: We thought Grandero Bello was going to have a great career, but he had a few little problems. We were hoping to go for the Kerry National but he didn't get in and the ground was too good in the Munster National. He's a proper winter horse. The owners are down the road from Newbury, so what was the Hennessy could be the next thing - Ricky Doyle, jockey.

runners.comment: 2-2 in handicap hurdles, up 10lb for easy win latest, could be more to come; cheekpieces
runners.spotlight: British challenger is 2-2 since tackling handicaps; won a three runner race at Doncaster (16.5f, gd-sft) off 106 then won in emphatic style at Wincanton upped to 2m4f (gd-sft) off 2lb higher; hiked up 10lb and moves up in grade but could be more to come; cheekpieces go on.

stable_tour.quote: He's grand and I like him. He's a homebred of Jean Sillett and was named after her husband John, who managed Coventry City to win the FA Cup in 1987. He was in junior hurdles last season and was second and third before parting company with Freddie Gordon at Chepstow. He can come back and run in a bumper because he's not won yet, although he wants to get on and stay over hurdles. 21-10-25

runners.comment: Market Rasen novice winner, beaten off this mark in first two h'caps, needs more
runners.spotlight: British challenger won a novice at Market Rasen on his second start; third off this mark in both handicaps, over 24.5f at Haydock and 21.5f at Wetherby; needs to find a bit more.

runners.breeder: S A S I E I , S C E A Des Prairies, M Khalifa Mohamed Al Att
runners.comment: 0-10, runner up in five of last six inc' twice here, place shout back in handicap company
runners.spotlight: Ten-race maiden over hurdles; runner up in five of his last six starts, including in handicaps here at 2m3f and 2m5f; beaten 9.5l in maidens the last twice at Navan and Clonmel; place shout returned to handicap company.

stable_tour.quote: A nice young horse who came from France and disappointed us initially on his first few starts. The break has done him good, though, and I think you'll see an improved animal when he reappears in a maiden hurdle soon. 26-10-25

runners.comment: Won on h'cap debut on latest, up 6lb and these are deeper waters, cheekpieces go on
runners.spotlight: Off the mark on handicap debut at Down Royal (20.5f, yielding) on latest off 111 (Accustomed 0.75l behind in second); raised 6lb for that and these are deeper waters; cheekpieces go on.

prev_owners.owner: J Carthy & Paul Byrne & Patrick John O'Brien

runners.comment: 1-17 over hurdles, no match for Laughing John on penultimate, new headgear combo
runners.spotlight: Flat winner is 1-17 over hurdles, the win coming in a Sedgefield maiden on latest (2m4f, good); previously proved no match for Laughing John in a handicap at Wincanton and work to do to turn that form around in new headgear.

runners.comment: Roscommon maiden hurdle winner, below best latest, better ground could help
runners.spotlight: Off the mark in a Roscommon maiden hurdle last September (15.5f, gd-yld); respectable run on handicap debut here in November (19.5f, heavy) but disappointed in a stronger race at Limerick (2m, sft-hvy) when last seen; may do better back on a sounder surface.

quotes.race: Athleague Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: I was able to get a position I wanted on Rakki and keep it as straightforward as I could. He's probably done well to sort himself out and find a leg there [following a mistake at the second-last] and his experience probably showed back in maiden company. He's done it nicely and he'll have to keep improving - Paul Townend, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He was a hand smaller than the first two when he third on his jumping debut at Chepstow and he acquitted himself well enough to suggest he can win over hurdles, although he was a shade disappointing at Warwick on Tuesday. He'll stay well and although he could boil over beforehand on the Flat I hope hurdling might put some manners on him. 07-11-24

runners.comment: Maiden hurdle winner, placed in both h'cap starts since, blinkers could eke out more
runners.spotlight: Justified short odds to win a Fairyhouse maiden hurdle in November (2m, sft-hvy); placed in both handicap hurdle starts since, over this C&D (sft-hvy) and back at Fairyhouse (2m4f, yld-sft); new blinkers could eke out more; player.

quotes.race: Sign Up To GavinLynchRacing.com Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Happy enough, Sticwiththeprocess didn't do a whole lot when he got to the front, he's a lairy so and so. He's a 114-rated horse and so you'd have to be a 120 or so giving him the 8lb allowance. Gordon (Elliott)'s horse (Whinney Hill) didn't operate at all so I'd say he ran up to his mark. If he switches on there may be a few more in him - Ted Walsh, trainer, speaking to Racing TV

runners.owner: Mrs P Bond, Magniers, Mrs P Shanahan
runners.comment: Maiden, behind a couple of these at Wetherby latest, likely capable of better
runners.spotlight: Maiden has run his best two races on good ground; beaten 7.75l when fourth behind a couple of these in a qualifier for this race at Wetherby last time; likely capable of better and can't discount.

stable_tour.quote: He went a bit weak on us after running with promise at Chepstow, but there's been no major issues. He's a big horse who has taken time to fill his frame, but he's done well over the summer and is one we're looking forward to seeing over hurdles. 18-11-25

prev_owners.owner: J Carthy & Paul Byrne & Patrick John O'Brien

runners.comment: 2-19, 8l behind Laughing John in qualifier, modest Flat run latest, others preferred
runners.spotlight: Four-time Flat winner is 2-19 over hurdles; 8l behind Laughing John when runner up in qualifier for this at Wincanton on penultimate; modest run on the level at Musselburgh on latest; others make more appeal.

quotes.race: Back The Super Boost At BetVictor Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Almuhit has improved so much and, although the wind op made a difference, switching from hurdles back to the Flat seems to have freshened him up - Faye Bramley, trainer.

runners.comment: 1-16 over hurdles, needs to bounce back from poor Fairyhouse run on latest
runners.spotlight: 1-16 over hurdles; ran well when a close third at Cork off 1lb higher on penultimate (2m4f, yielding); needs to bounce back from disappointing Fairyhouse run latest; others look better treated.

runners.owner: J T O'Connor & M P Gleeson & P M Fortune & A McGonigle

prev_owners.owner: J T O'Connor & M P Gleeson & P M Fortune & A McGonigle

runners.comment: 0-5 over hurdles, 3.5l behind Powerful here latest (2m5f), up 3lb, drop in trip a query
runners.spotlight: 0-5 over hurdles; best run yet on handicap debut here on latest when a 3.5l third of 15 behind Powerful (2m5f, sft-hvy); 3lb rise for that seems a touch harsh and not sure this drop in trip will suit.

runners.comment: 3-26 over hurdles, runner up the last twice, may be vulnerable to less exposed sorts
runners.spotlight: 3-26 over hurdles; runner up the last twice, off 5lb lower at Leopardstown and then off 3lb lower at Cork when 1.5l behind Onlymammycanloveme; weighted to turn that around but may be vulnerable to less exposed sorts.

runners.comment: Three-time chase winner, 0-23 over hurdles, new cheekpieces need to eke out more
runners.spotlight: Three-time chase winner is 0-23 over hurdles; rated 12lb lower in this sphere but failed to exploit his lesser mark on last start over timber at Gowran; cheekpieces need to eke out more.

quotes.race: Tim & Martin Molony Veterans Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: He is overdue another win. Krabat ran over hurdles for his first run back. He got a bit of an injury last year, so he was out for a while, and he came back a better horse than he was last year. He came back looking thin and shook, but he progressed well, so sometimes I think when they come back heavy, it takes too much work to get them ready. If he keeps going that way, he'll go okay. It was a nice race to win - Michael McDonagh, trainer.

runners.comment: 1-9 over hurdles, behind a couple of these at Cork latest, might prefer softer ground
runners.spotlight: 1-9 over hurdles; attempted to make all when finishing behind a couple of these at Cork latest (2m4f, yielding); probably up against it in this company and might prefer softer ground than this.

runners.comment: Scottish raider, good placed efforts last twice, can't discount in first-time cheekpieces
runners.spotlight: Scottish raider; 0-5 but getting closer with each run this season; 2.5l behind Judicial Deference on penultimate at Kelso (22.5f, heavy); beaten a neck at Hexham on latest (2m4f, soft); cheekpieces go on now; can't discount.

runners.comment: Went close off 1lb lower at Huntingdon in Jan', ground too quick latest, could outrun odds
runners.spotlight: British challenger; dual-purpose; has won on the AW on the Flat but is 0-10 over hurdles; went close off 1lb lower at Huntingdon (20.5f, soft) in January; ground may have been too lively at Southwell latest; could outrun his odds back on easier ground.

runners.breeder: S C E A Haras Du Puy
runners.comment: 2-29 over hurdles, recent form disappointing, major revival needed
runners.spotlight: Three-time chase winner is 2-29 over hurdles; rated 13lb lower over timber but recent form in both codes has been disappointing and a major revival is needed.

quotes.race: www.thurlesraces.ie Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Union Park was very fizzy in his early days but it is only now that he is starting to settle and getting the hang of it. He definitely seems to be going the right way - Philip Rothwell, trainer.

quotes.race: Jossestown Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Union Park deserved to win that, it has been a little bit frustrating. We decided to wait for this race instead of running at Cork last week as he was coming back to 2m - Philip Rothwell, trainer.

quotes.race: West Tyre Ballintubber & Westport Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: We will see how Union Park comes out of this. His owner would love a runner in Galway, and he is entered in a few of the handicaps there, but it might come a bit soon - Philip Rothwell, trainer.

runners.comment: Narrowly denied on penultimate, pulled up latest, blinkers on, 2lb wrong
runners.spotlight: Good run when a 3.5l sixth at Leopardstown in December and narrowly denied on his next start at Down Royal (20.5f, yielding); pulled up on latest at Wexford, however, and needs to bounce back in first-time blinkers; 2lb wrong.

runners.owner: David L'Estrange & Eric Newnham & William Esdaile
runners.comment: Much improved on h'cap debut latest, this tougher and 2lb wrong but can't dismiss
runners.spotlight: Much improved effort on handicap debut at Down Royal in March when a 1.25l third of 19; this much tougher and he's 2lb wrong but he's unexposed and can't be totally discounted.

runners.comment: Three-time Fairyhouse winner, back to form latest but vulnerable in this company; reserve
runners.spotlight: First reserve; all three previous wins at Fairyhouse; back to form when a 3.75l third behind Onlymammycanlove me at Cork on latest; probably vulnerable to younger legs.

quotes.race: Kevin Sheedy Bowel Cancer Raceday 17th December Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Whatsavailable will make a lovely chaser. The tongue tie worked well with him - Mouse Morris, trainer.

quotes.race: Mongey Communications Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Whatsavailable never runs a bad race, and he'll make some chaser next season - he gave the last about a foot. He had a bit of experience and you can't beat that - Mouse Morris, trainer

runners.breeder: Mme Clotilde Domenjoud & Haras De Saint Voir Sca
runners.comment: C&D winner in January, beaten off revised mark latest, others appeal more; reserve
runners.spotlight: Second reserve; won over C&D in January (heavy) off 90; has come up short twice since, in a listed handicap chase at Naas and back over hurdles at Cork last time; 2lb wrong and others make more appeal.

quotes.race: Prior Park Service Station Clonmel Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Kobalt St Georges was bound to come on a little bit from his win the last day but I thought two miles might catch him today but there was nothing else suitable coming up. I also didn't want to come back 14 days later either. We'll go steady now as he's run twice in 14 days and he'll probably go back hurdling at some stage, although he jumps so well that he mightn't be as effective back over hurdles - Robert Tyner, trainer.

racecards.verdict: It might be worth taking a chance on MOAB off a nice low weight with the return to easier ground in his favour.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/1 Daylatedollarshort,  Rakki, 8/1 Laughing John, 17/2 Sticwiththeprocess, 10/1 Moon Mission,  Matt Connor, 11/1 Onlymammycanloveme, 12/1 Powerful,  San Hilario,  Almuhit, 14/1 Freshers Week,  Onefortheditch,  Judicial Deference, 18/1 Pat's Legacy, 20/1 Bright Legend, 22/1 Assertive Walk,  Fairlander, 25/1 Moylussa,  Another High Five, 28/1 Moab, 33/1 Must Go Now,  Krabat,  Accustomed, 50/1 Grandero Bello, 66/1 Union Park

racecards.race_name: Killashee Hotel Handicap Hurdle (Listed Race)

runners.comment: Beaten fav' the last twice, reportedly stopped quickly on latest, Townend jumps ship
runners.spotlight: Arguably a shade unlucky when a beaten favourite in the County Hurdle but rider reported that he stopped quickly when soundly beaten at Fairyhouse last time; Townend jumps ship; needs to rediscover best.

quotes.race: 50,000 Euros BetVictor Graduation Bonus Series Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Karbau put up a very nice performance there. He came on a lot for his first run and his jumping was really good. He is entered in the Supreme and the Turners - Willie Mullins, trainer.

runners.breeder: Sarl De Chambure Haras D'Etreham Et Al
runners.comment: Grade 1 winner last year, no joy since but drying ground a plus, the choice of Townend
runners.spotlight: Grade 1 Juvenile winner at Aintree (2m1f, gd-sft) last year; has come up dry since, beaten similar distances in first three handicaps; dropped 1lb for an 11l fifth behind Kalix Delabarriere on latest and Townend takes over now; drying ground a plus and could go well.

quotes.race: Boodles Anniversary 4-Y-O Juvenile Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I wasn't expecting that! I was hoping better ground would make a difference, I was hoping Murcia would finish in the first four - you never know, looking at the drama in jump racing, between Cheltenham and whatever - anything can happen, and if you're not in it you can't win it. That was a big, improved performance; nicer ground, and physically the weight - she'd only 10st 9lb, I think she'd been carrying a lot more weight in her other races, and this was more a mares' weight, which was a huge advantage to her as well. She'll go to Punchestown as long as she comes out of it well, but she seems a tough mare - we haven't spared her this winter, and to come out and put in a career-best performance in April, that's a good sign, a great sign. I wondered if Paul had gone too soon, because it's a long way up that straight, especially from the last hurdle home, it's a long way, but he'd put it all to bed by then. There's a good programme for mares - we'll find something for her [next season]. She'll have a long holiday after Punchestown - unless we go to Auteuil! - Willie Mullins, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She came of age when winning the Grade 1 juvenile hurdle at Aintree. That was her best performance last season, although she also ran well back at Punchestown. The Mares' Hurdle will be her aim as I don't think she has the size for fences. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Grade 2 novice winner here over fences, rated 17lb lower over hurdles, can't discount
runners.spotlight: Talented chaser rated 152 in that sphere and a Grade 2 novice chase winner at this venue; soundly beaten in the Grand Annual on latest and now tries to exploit a 17lb lower hurdles mark on first start over timber since April 2024; can't discount.

quotes.race: Betfair Henry VIII Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Touch Me Not was travelling away and that one mistake [at the sixth] knocked the stuffing out of him. It knocked his confidence a small bit but he still ran a cracker. He was a little bit low at the second-last but over the last he was good. He's a young horse who is still learning and hopefully there's more big days ahead - Jordan Gainford, rider.

quotes.race: BetVictor Craddockstown Novice Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: We got Touch Me Not from the point-to-point field. He actually fell in his point-to-point, believe it or not. I was worried about the ground, but it was a good performance and he came on plenty from last time. He was very keen as a young horse and didn't show me anything. He was well down the pecking order, but he's come a long way in six months. He might not be easy to place at Christmas. The two-mile race at Leopardstown is not there anymore and I don't think the Grade 1 at Limerick would suit. We'll get him home and see - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I couldn't believe how well he took to fences. He surprised everybody, including me. Because he was so good at it and won a Grade 2 at Punchestown, he spent the rest of the season in Grade 1s. That wasn't easy for him but he ran some big races. He might not be the easiest horse to place this season with his rating but he'll probably start off in the Fortria Chase at the Navan racing festival and we'll take it from there. 26-10-25

runners.comment: Back to form with a bang at Fairyhouse under this rider latest, obvious chance with repeat
runners.spotlight: Back to form with a bang at Fairyhouse under this rider latest, winning by 5l with a few of these behind; a 9lb rise for that seems fair but overall profile suggests he's far from guaranteed to back that up; obvious chance if he does.

runners.comment: Won off 8lb lower in Nov', has fallen two of last three starts, risky proposition for now
runners.spotlight: Won off 8lb lower at Navan in November and good third at Leopardstown off revised mark the following month; has fallen in two of last three starts, however, so he's a risky proposition for now.

quotes.race: QuinnBet Handicap Hurdle (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Balko D'Ange missed a few hurdles last time, which is unlike him. He's generally quick at his hurdles. We were disappointed with him then, but then you look at what the winner has done since. He was in off a nice mark and has the look of a horse who will get better with racing. Putting him into a good handicap off a low weight is the way we're probably thinking. The big handicap hurdles at the Dublin Racing Festival might just be a bit competitive for him at this stage; we'd like to take it step by step - Philip Fenton, trainer.

prev_owners.owner: Exors of the Late Jeremiah Nolan

runners.comment: Admirable dual-purpose veteran, time may be catching up on evidence of last two runs
runners.spotlight: Admirable dual-purpose veteran is a winner of 14 races; 6-34 over hurdles but time may be catching up with him based on the evidence of his last two runs and was well beaten in this in 2024 off 2lb lower.

quotes.race: Executive Helicopters Handicap
quotes.quote: Lord Erskine is as enthusiastic as ever. He pulled my arms out going down to the start, and even though we weren't going mad early he was still taking me along. I knew he would stay well and Harry [Rogers, trainer] said he'd love it round here - Ronan Whelan, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.race: RYBO Handicap Hurdle (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: You'd think Lord Erskine would be getting slower as he gets older and I thought they weren't going fast enough there and I was worried about the ground, but he proved me wrong. He's a great horse to have. I didn't believe he would ever win another race, but he has. He might end up in Punchestown, we'll see. He might go to Killarney for something on the Flat if he's still enjoying it - Harry Rogers, trainer.

quotes.race: Timeless Sash Windows Handicap Hurdle (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I was a bit worried about the ground but Darragh (O'Keeffe) said it was no problem. I could never get Lord Erskine into a good race with a light weight and it was the same on the Flat. He'd a proper weight on his back today and there was a good gallop which suited him. His (late) owner Jerry Nolan was a pure gentleman. I rode winners for him and having an owner like him, you couldn't buy them - Harry Rogers, trainer.

quotes.race: Friends Of The Curragh Pollardstown Handicap
quotes.quote: We ran Lord Erskine at Listowel the other day and it just didn't work out. He does want two miles and that ground. I stuck the blinkers on him on Friday morning and that made the difference but he loves that ground and the trip. He's just easy to train and he's very laid-back, that's what's wrong with him, he just does what he wants and doesn't kill himself - Harry Rogers, trainer

quotes.race: Treo Eile Retraining Ireland's Racehorses Handicap
quotes.quote: We had to resort to plan B as Lord Erskine missed the break and had to sacrifice a couple of lengths to get him to the outside, but it worked out thankfully. That is his minimum trip as he is slow, but full of stamina. He was owned by the late Jerry Nolan and I'm delighted for connections - Harry is a big supporter of mine and himself and Miriam work very hard. I'm delighted for them. He is a yard stalwart, loves the track and is as genuine as they come.  - Siobhan Rutledge, rider.

quotes.race: BetVictor Run For Your Money Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: He's a decent horse on his day but he's had problems and it's just taken a long time to get him back. He was a bit keen today and the jumping seemed to wake him up a little bit. He handles that ground well and stays well. Hopefully things stay right with him, it's a long time since he won the Irish Cesarewitch here. He'll keep on going over the winter - Harry Rogers, trainer of Lord Erskine

quotes.race: Ryans Cleaning Event Specialists Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Lord Erskine is a nice horse and hopefully he can get another one. He's in again at Clonmel next week so we'll see how he comes out of this - Harry Rogers, trainer.

quotes.race: Strandhill Caravan Park Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: He's 18 in the ballot at Tipperary but that might bring him up a bit. He'll probably stay over hurdles for a while. He wants a dig in the ground and he wouldn't want it any quicker than that. Hopefully he might end up at Galway and if all goes well he'd scrape into the amateur race - Harry Rogers, trainer

quotes.race: Irish Cesarewitch (Premier Handicap)
quotes.quote: He was weak when we got him but he has progressed very well. They went a decent gallop and that suited him. He's a good horse and we might head for the Naas November Handicap next. He does like a good ease in the ground - Harry Rogers, trainer

quotes.race: John & Terry Moriarty Memorial Handicap
quotes.quote: He wouldn't be in love with the ground but he got away with it. When they get off in front here it seems to be hard to catch them. He's in at Ballinrobe next Thursday over hurdles but he hasn't really taken to hurdles so far. We might be better off keeping him on the Flat and go back over hurdles next year -  Harry Rogers, trainer

quotes.race: Sean Cleary Memorial Handicap
quotes.quote: He was unlucky in Tramore, Rachael Blackmore gave him a good ride but he was just too free. The plan was always to come here and when Pat Smullen is available, it's a help. He done it well and he's in at Navan on Saturday, where if there's any rain, he'll probably take his chance. The handicapper might give him 5lb or 6lb - Harry Rogers, trainer

runners.comment: 2-7 over hurdles, Gr' 3 mares' novice winner, poor at Cheltenham latest, needs to rebound
runners.spotlight: Handicap debutante; 2-7 over hurdles and made all to land a Grade 3 mares' novice at Down Royal on her penultimate start (2m1f, gd-yld); well beaten in mares' novice at Cheltenham on latest; needs to bounce back.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Feathard Lady Mares Novice Hurdle (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Fair play to owner Roger Kissane as he suggested this. Darragh [O'Keefe] gave her some spin, Full Of Life is brilliant to jump and she's exciting. I'd say we just got the trip wrong previously but we'll stay hurdling for this season and she'll be a nice novice chaser next season - Henry De Bromhead, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She's been off since October but she worked really well recently. She came back over hurdles on her last run and beat Carrigmoornaspruce, who franked the form when second in a Grade 1 next time. She'll go for the Mares' Novices' Hurdle. 15-02-26

runners.breeder: Elevage Du Colombier, Haras De Saint-Voi
runners.comment: Bad mistake costly on handicap bow at Kelso latest, could go well if jumps better
runners.spotlight: British raider; dual Grade 3 bumper winner in France; won two of first four starts over hurdles for this yard but a bad mistake two out proved costly when pulled up on handicap debut at Kelso latest; could go well if puts in a clear round of jumping.

quotes.race: Support The Injured Jockeys Fund Mares' Novices' Hurdle (Herring Queen Mares' Nov' Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: We were only hacking around. Khrisma was very professional, she's grown up so much in the last year or so and she's really come on for that race at Punchestown - Nico De Boinville, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: I like her and she has had some solid AQPS Flat form in France. She needed to learn to settle last season but, amazingly for a horse who pulled so hard at home, she was great on the racecourse when she finished third at Windsor and second at Punchestown. She travelled into the race in Ireland like a good horse and got beaten by a hotpot. She's still a novice over hurdles and she's well educated. 21-10-25

runners.comment: Progress has stalled since back-to-back wins and Gr' 3 place, soundly beaten last thrice
runners.spotlight: Won his first two starts, a bumper at Fairyhouse last April and a Cork maiden hurdle on his seasonal return in November; 7.5l second in Fairyhouse Grade 3 later that month but soundly beaten in three runs since, including in handicaps last twice; more needed.

runners.comment: Won at Chepstow off 1lb higher in Oct', heavy defeats four starts since, hard to fancy
runners.spotlight: Won well on seasonal return at Chepstow in October off 128 and 1lb lower now but he's suffered heavy defeats on his four starts since that success; leap of faith required to back him here.

quotes.race: Bar One Racing "100% Football Acca Boost On Self Service Betting Terminals" Handicap Hurdle (Listed)
quotes.quote: Washington won at Chepstow and I considered the Greatwood but I thought Cheltenham would not suit us at all. I knew this big galloping track would be perfect for him. It's very very rare in horse racing that a plan comes together but this one actually did - Harry Derham, trainer

quotes.race: 3 As Leisure Motorhome-Caravan Sales Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Paul [O'Brien] gave Washington a good ride. I'm very pleased with him - he's been with us a while and taken time to come right, so I'm glad he has rewarded the patience of his owners - Harry Derham, trainer.

quotes.race: MansionBet Cheltmas Bet £10 Get £20 Standard Open National Hunt Flat Race (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was a very strong performance from Washington as it's difficult to win these races under a penalty. He was keen enough early on but came through well in the end although I may well have gone too soon - Lewis Stones, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He's sort of already done his bit for the season in winning at Chepstow. He could go to Doncaster in the middle of December for a two-mile hurdle. He's nearly at a career-high mark again now, so it makes life harder for him. We could freshen him up and have a crack at one of the spring festivals as he likes top of the ground. 19-11-25

He's a nice type but I was very disappointed with his recent effort at Newbury, where he was pulled up. I'm not sure if it was the fitting of a hood or the fact he was dropped in, prompting him to sulk. We'll go back to 2m next time with a more positive ride and see if that sparks him back to life. The positive is that he's around his last winning rating. 22-12-22

runners.owner: John P McManus & Mrs John Magnier

prev_owners.owner: Mrs John Magnier & John P McManus

runners.comment: Yet to build on early promise, soundly beaten on h'cap debut latest, tongue tie tried now
runners.spotlight: Looked a smart prospect last year but has failed to deliver in three runs this term, although was highly tried in his first two runs of 2026; never figured on handicap debut at Fairyhouse latest; down 2lb and tongue tie now reached for.

quotes.race: Galway Bay Hotel & The Galmont Hotel Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: He was a bit novicey, we were trapping down to the second last and Davy Crockett got a bit unsighted and just galloped into it. I loved the way he picked up after that and winged the last. Plenty of improvement likely. He had been keen in his bumper but settled grand until he got a bit lit up in second half of the race. He'll learn in time, he's not a big horse but there's an engine in there - Mark Walsh, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He'll be back for the second half of the season. He's out on a break at the moment. I would be thinking about something like the Moscow Flyer at Punchestown in February. I loved the way he jumped and attacked his hurdles when he won at Galway and Listowel, he looked as though he'd been doing it all his life. I know they were early season races, but I think he's good enough to be aimed at Grade 1 novice hurdles. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Good effort in Imperial Cup on penultimate, place chance if repeats that form
runners.spotlight: Dual-purpose; 1-10 over hurdles; good effort at big odds when a 4.5l fourth of 18 in the Imperial Cup at Sandown in March; didn't back that up at Fairyhouse on latest; would have a place chance with a repeat of that Sandown run.

quotes.race: Renvyle House Hotel 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Messerschmitt has been a very unlucky horse but I think he's a good horse. He stays well and he loves jumping, he's a good size and very athletic. I would imagine he will go on to the graded race at Fairyhouse - Noel Meade, trainer

quotes.race: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: It was a messy sort of race and I tried to keep things as smooth as I could. Messerschmitt is a lovely-moving horse and I think there'll be plenty of improvement on nicer ground - Ben Coen, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

runners.comment: Held form well since Huntingdon win inc' third in Imperial Cup, in the mix; cheekpieces on
runners.spotlight: Has held form well since scoring at Huntingdon in December off 9lb lower; good third in Imperial Cup on penultimate and 4l runner up at Haydock off 1lb lower on latest; in the mix again with cheekpieces an interesting addition.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Handicap Hurdle (Challenger Two Mile Hurdle Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: We had one just get beat yesterday and that was our first winner since we opened the yard back up again. They seem in good form, but they take a while to get back. I know from the past if you don't stop you do more harm than good so we gave them three weeks there just to freshen them up and hopefully we can get going again. We're Red And Blue is quite a nice horse and that was more like it from him today. He did everything right today as he jumped well and kept going well. He did the job well, but it is just nice seeing them come back to form - Jonjo O'Neill, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He beat Jet To Vegas, who went on to win a Grade 2, when winning at Carlisle last season, and was beaten only five lengths in the Imperial Cup. He's still a young horse, but that experience will hopefully help him this season. He wants a fence, but off 116 we hope there's a bit of mileage over hurdles first. He wasn't himself at Aintree on his comeback, but we're hopeful he can progress this season. 18-11-25

runners.comment: 1-10 over hurdles, well beaten when last seen in November, others appeal more
runners.spotlight: Dual-purpose; 1-10 over hurdles; soundly beaten off 2lb higher when last seen at Down Royal in November; others make more appeal.

stable_tour.quote: He looked like he was coming to win at Cheltenham on Friday but probably didn't quite get home over that trip. We'll go back to two miles with him and he should be very competitive in some nice handicap hurdles. 26-10-25

runners.comment: Dual-purpose, won at this meeting last year under Bowen, Flat win latest, can't discount
runners.spotlight: Dual-purpose; 2-8 over hurdles, his last win coming at this meeting last year off 7lb lower; no impact over timber since but won on the Flat at Bellewstown 17 days ago and Sean Bowen was on board for that win here last season; can't discount.

quotes.race: Specialist Group Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I hope Putapoundinthejar will keep improving. He should make a chaser in time, he's a typical Walk In The Park, he can be a little on edge but as soon he's cantering he's very straightforward. He wants better ground and could head to Galway - Tony Martin, trainer, speaking to Racing TV

quotes.race: Molson Coors Beverage Company Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: It has just taken a while for everything to fall into place. Putapoundinthejar is still relatively young and immature. Today's race turned into a great opportunity with Willie's not there. We always thought he was a nice young horse and we still do - Tony Martin, trainer.

runners.comment: Maiden and novice hurdle winner, yet to fire in h'caps, pulled up latest, others preferred
runners.spotlight: Dual-purpose; maiden and novice hurdle winner has yet to fire in handicaps; pulled up when 40-1 at Cork on latest; others hold more pressing claims.

runners.comment: Raised 9lb for easy handicap debut win at Fairyhouse, unexposed, may be more to come
runners.spotlight: Promise in maiden hurdles and ran out an easy winner on handicap debut at Fairyhouse three weeks ago (2m, yld-sft); raised 9lb and this is tougher but he's unexposed and there could be plenty more to come.

runners.comment: No win since Sept' 2024, off since last June, 1lb wrong, rider's claim a plus
runners.spotlight: No joy since winning a listed handicap hurdle at Listowel in September 2024 off 6lb lower; 1lb wrong here and lacks a recent run; rider's claim a plus but others make more appeal.

runners.comment: Improved effort on h'cap bow latest, this shorter trip a plus, 1lb wrong but a player
runners.spotlight: Better effort on handicap debut at Cork (2m3f, yielding) on latest, travelling strongly before weakening in the closing stages; 1lb wrong here but it's early days and this shorter trip should suit; player.

stable_tour.quote: I expected more from him at Cheltenham and Punchestown last season, but he probably just wasn't mature enough for those races. He's done well over the summer and seems to have grown up. He's a chaser down the line, but we'll stick to novice hurdles this season and he could be one for handicaps later in the campaign. 17-11-25

runners.breeder: Mme Nathalie Viel & Mr Matheo Viel
runners.comment: Won easily on h'cap debut at Fairyhouse, beaten off revised mark latest, wants it softer
runners.spotlight: French bumper winner; 4yo won easily on handicap bow at Fairyhouse in February (16.5f, heavy); came up short off 14lb higher back there on latest when 1lb wrong and similar story here; would probably prefer softer ground.

runners.comment: Course winner, in decent form, beaten 3.25l on latest, 4lb wrong here, minor place shout
runners.spotlight: Course winner in decent form and has finished in the first four in four of five starts this season; beaten 3.25l behind Sainte Lucie at Cork on latest; cheekpieces worn that day left off and he's 4lb wrong here; minor place claims.

quotes.race: Connolly's RED MILLS Irish EBF Auction Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Rockymountainbeau had a good run in a point-to-point and his work at home has been good. We knew he'd be competitive but didn't know whether he needed the run but he did it well. It will sharpen him up a lot as he was looking for a bit of company - Tiernan Power Roche, rider, speaking to Racing TV.

racecards.verdict: JET TO MONTE CARLO is preferred. He bolted up on his handicap debut last time and a 9lb rise may not stop him from following up
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/2 Murcia, 6/1 Khrisma, 7/1 Jet To Monte Carlo, 10/1 Kalix Delabarriere, 11/1 Davy Crockett,  Larzac, 12/1 Karbau,  Touch Me Not, 14/1 Full Of Life,  We're Red And Blue,  Putapoundinthejar,  Rockymountainbleu, 16/1 I'm Slippy, 20/1 Messerschmitt, 22/1 Frankendael, 25/1 Arch Empire,  Mode Avion, 33/1 Balko d'Ange, 40/1 Washington,  Lord Erskine, 50/1 Autumn Twist

racecards.race_name: PRL Champion Novice Hurdle (Grade 1)

prev_owners.owner: Miss E Nolan And Paul Hancock

runners.comment: Closely matched with Koktail Brut and Le Labo, go close with clear round of jumping
runners.spotlight: Flat winner; won impressively on hurdles debut at Down Royal and then touched off in the Royal Bond by Koktail Brut; further behind that rival in DRF Grade 1 and beaten a neck by Le Labo in Grade 3 at Naas; still in the mix when falling at the last at Fairyhouse last time in first-time cheekpieces (discarded); can go close with a clear round.

quotes.race: Tayto Group Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
quotes.quote: Blake was magic. He jumped so well, Donagh [Meyler] said he jumped so well all the time and he was able to take him back so he was full of running. When he said go to him, he absolutely exploded on him. He's a big, tall, leggy horse who improved a lot from last spring. I know he was beaten in that race at Leopardstown, but he was stopped to a walk. Chris [Hayes] said he thought he would have won. I suppose the Royal Bond is a possibibility for him or something like that. I don't know, we will see. I just think he is a leggy horse and I don't think he needs to get too much racing. He could be decent - Noel Meade, trainer.

quotes.race: Bahrain Turf Club October Handicap (Premier Handicap)
quotes.quote: To be honest, they nearly had to give it to Blake. You can't stop them to that degree, can you? They absolutely stopped him and he's a big, long-striding horse. If you're riding a bike and you're stopped, it's very hard to get going again that quickly. It's a nice pot to win and he'll run in the maiden hurdle at Down Royal on Saturday week. That's the plan. He jumps great and we're looking forward to him heading over hurdles - Noel Meade, trainer.

runners.comment: Has come up well short in two previous runs in graded races, hood goes on
runners.spotlight: Both wins have come when ridden from the front, a Galway maiden hurdle and a Thurles handicap off 124; has come up well short in both previous runs in graded company; now tried in a hood; others preferred.

quotes.race: Most Stylish Racegoers Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Plan A was to go and win the Royal Bond. It just didn't happen for him on the day. A few of ours were running below par, and the ball has bounced back now. That's him. Eachtotheirown is not really a frontrunner. I just said there's going to be no pace today, so just buck him out and if somebody wants to take it off him, then well and good. I don't know what he's run to there. I think he's top class, so what's he going to get, 8 or 10lbs? So about 132, he'd have a nice handicap mark if we wanted to avail of that. We'll see, we could either do that, or we could look at a graded race. I'll have a chat with Tim and we'll see.   [Would you be tempted by the Supreme?] I might. Sure, if we won the Royal Bond, that's where we would've been going. Now it looks a hot race this year but look at the size of him, he's going to be a chaser next year. [Could he go up in trip for a Turners?] No, no, he's all speed. We're delighted to have him back to what we thought he was - Barry Connell, trainer, talking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Didn't get home in the Supreme, this track more suitable, big chance if jumps well
runners.spotlight: One of three for yard; smart bumper form; fell with race at his mercy on hurdles debut at Leopardstown in December; survived a final flight blunder to win a maiden at Thurles; didn't get home up the Cheltenham hill in the Supreme last time; this track should suit better; preferred by Kennedy and big chance if cutting out the jumping errors.

quotes.race: ThurlesRaces.ie Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: El Cairos never came out of second gear. Jack [Kennedy] said it was his own fault as he went down to the last and said he should have taken him back or asked him, but he did neither and the horse galloped up on it. I loved the way he came back on it straight away, you'd have to be impressed with that. I was nervous about the ground as we came looking for good ground. Had we not run today, it would have had to have been Punchestown or Navan next week, and that's getting close to Cheltenham. He's very fast and Jack says the boot he has is unreal, even on that [heavy] ground. He'd have learned plenty and the big field would have done him no harm. He'll go straight to Cheltenham now. He jumped brilliantly the whole way bar the last - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Thorntons Recycling Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: El Cairos is 100 per cent. He looked good and I'd say he's a proper horse. We'll get him home and make sure he's all okay but 'd say we'll have one more run and then the Supreme, that'd be the plan. He looks nice - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: British Horse Society Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: El Cairos was impressive and he's a nice horse. He's always shown that at home, but the proof is in the pudding here today and it was a rare turn of foot - Gary Moore, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: This chap is rapid. We haven't had too many quicker than him at Cullentra. Jack [Kennedy] blamed himself for what happened at the last at Thurles. He just felt he didn't ask him to do one thing or the other. Before that, he'd jumped great and settled well in a slowly run race. I wanted to go for a race like that at Thurles, rather than a Grade 1 at the Dublin Racing Festival, just to get his confidence up. He's working great, looks great and we're looking forward to the Supreme. It's going to be one hell of a hot race but it'll take a fair one to beat him.  09-02-26

runners.comment: French winner, has come up short on first two runs for Willie Mullins, more needed
runners.spotlight: One of three for yard; French recruit; won on second start for Daniela Mele at Dieppe (2m1f, soft); last of three over C&D in Grade 2 on Irish debut; never involved when 100-1 in the Supreme last time; major improvement required.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Moscow Flyer Novice Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: I think Free Spirit will improve loads. Obviously he's a completely different type having had just the two hurdles races in France but he jumped well and kept galloping - David Casey, assistant trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I liked what I saw from him in France and he could be a nice novice hurdler this season. He's by Muhtathir, so he could be sharp. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Dual Grade 2 winner, closely matched with Blake, drying track would be a slight worry
runners.spotlight: One of three for yard; bright start over timber, winning a C&D maiden (heavy) and beating Blake by a head in the Royal Bond; limitations seemingly exposed in Grade 1 company on his next three runs but back on song with a Grade 2 win at Fairyhouse last time (left in lead after Blake fell at the last); wouldn't want the track to dry out too much.

quotes.race: Donohue Marquees Novice Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Koktail Brut is a good horse, he was giving a penalty away there. It was nip and tuck down to the last, but Jack thought he had the beating of Blake and I thought it was a good performance. He could be a nice chaser next season. He was bought to be a big chaser down the road. He's a lovely horse for the future - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Bar 1 Betting Royal Bond Novice Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Koktail Brut did everything wrong probably as Jack said he was keen enough in front. We weren't sure if there was going to be pace in the race, so we said we'd keep it simple and go on. He was very gutsy to come back. Looking at that, I'd say a bit further would suit him. I'll talk to Michael and Eddie [O'Leary] and see, but we won't just say he definitely wants two and a half miles yet. He could be one to keep and go to the Lawlor's of Naas - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Bar One Racing "Bet Builder On Self Service Betting Terminals" (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: I'd say Koktail Brut is a nice horse. We thought we had a few nice ones at home and that was a good performance. He's a bit faster than his half-brother Gevrey and shows a bit of class. I'd imagine we'll look for a Graded bumper - Gordon Elliott, trainer

stable_tour.quote: This guy isn't short of pace and did well in bumpers. He's one to look forward to over hurdles and is ready to start. You'll see him very soon. 26-10-25

runners.comment: Failed to complete first two starts over timber, beat Blake in Gr'3 latest, go well again
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner; mishaps first two runs over timber, unseating at the first at Thurles then falling with the race at his mercy at Cork; put in a clear round last time in a Grade 3 at Naas (16.5f, sft-hvy) and lowered the colours of Blake by a neck; should go well again if as effective on this quicker ground (bumper win on good).

quotes.race: BAR 1 Betting "Better Prices On Self-Service Betting Terminals" Kingsfurze Novice Hurdle (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: He's a horse that we've always liked. We decided to go here today, with a smaller field, to give Le Labo another nice experience and if it happened, it happened. Thankfully it did. I was quite happy to follow. I thought the pace was even and the ground is a bit dead. He's a horse with a nice turn of foot, and I'd say, a nice touch of class as well. I think he's a horse that's going to keep improving and he's one for the future - John Gleeson, jockey.

runners.comment: Point, maiden hurdle and Gr' 1 winner, trip too far on latest, could rebound; hooded
runners.spotlight: One of three for stable; point winner; beaten in sole bumper and on hurdles debut at Gowran in early November; off the mark in a maiden at Fairyhouse later that month and took the step up to Grade 1 company in his stride at Leopardstown's Christmas meeting, winning by 5l; beaten when falling in the 2m5f Turners at Cheltenham; this trip more suitable and could bounce back in the first time hood.

quotes.race: Paddy Power Future Champions Novice Hurdle (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Skylight Hustle travelled like a dream the whole way and jumped like a buck. I thought looking at it live, we were beat, but when I look at the rerun, I'm not sure given the way my lad galloped from the back of the last to the line. Jack [Kennedy] said he couldn't guarantee he would've won, but he said he wasn't beaten. He really liked him. It's unfortunate for Joseph's horse [Talk The Talk], but thankfully he's up okay. He's a good horse. He's quick, but I think he'll stay further as well. I'd imagine he could come back for the Dublin Racing Festival - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We thought he was one of our best bumper horses last season, but he didn't run the way I hoped he would at Fairyhouse. It's been much more like it this season and he's already a Grade 1 winner. I know people said he was lucky against Talk The Talk, and he probably was, but Jack said he really hit the line hard, so I think the Turners is made for him. He's a very classy horse who always works well. He had three quick runs before Christmas, so we've freshened him up for Cheltenham. 09-02-26

runners.owner: Oti Racing & The Why Knot Partnership
runners.comment: Classy on Flat, C&D Grade 2 winner, poor latest but could rebound, preferred by Townend
runners.spotlight: One of three for yard; Group 2 winner on the Flat for Andre Fabre and won the Queen Alexandra for this stable at Ascot; bright start over hurdles, winning a 2m4f Killarney novice (yielding) and a Grade 2 novice over this C&D (sft-hvy); jumped poorly and well beaten stepped up to Grade 1 company in the Turners at Cheltenham; capable of better than that and notable that he is the choice of Townend.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Moscow Flyer Novice Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: It was a bit cat and mouse but Sober had a bit of class at the end of it and quickened well. He had a little look at the last but sorted himself out and was doing enough. He's a good individual. It had been such a tactical affair I didn't want to go to the last a length down and miss it. I wanted to put it to bed. He travelled better and sweeter, I also think he enjoyed this a lot more. It was a nice performance. He can improve plenty but I like the willingness he showed and he had a good experience - Paul Townend, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Queen Alexandra Stakes (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Sober has surprised us; he's improved a lot more than I thought he would. We will aim for the Melbourne Cup - this was stage one. There are a lot of hoops to jump through, but we'll get them done - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Examiner Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: Sober has got loads of ability and hopefully hurdling will just sharpen him up. I was losing a length at a lot of hurdles and he hangs a bit. He will jump well in time and I'd say it was a good performance to win - Paul Townend, jockey.

quotes.race: Sumbe Prix Kergorlay (Group 2) (3yo+) (Round Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: I have no idea if Sober will step up in distance for the Prix du Cadran, but he finished the race still moving forward. We'll see if we try that or wait for the Prix Royal-Oak - Pierre-Yves Bureau, racing manager for the Wertheimers.

stable_tour.quote: He's back in training now after a break and he could be one that we will train with the Turners Novices' Hurdle in mind next March. He's a classy individual. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Useful on Flat, struggled up in class since C&D maiden win, overlooked by Townend
runners.spotlight: One of three for yard; Useful on the Flat; off the mark over hurdles in a C&D maiden in February (sft-hvy); beaten 11.5l when midfield in the Supreme at Cheltenham (when Townend rode) and raced keenly before pulled up in the Fairyhouse Grade 2 won by Koktail Brut latest; overlooked by Townend here.

stable_tour.quote: I really liked his run in the Triumph Hurdle. He impressed me there. I wanted to win a nice Flat handicap with him over the summer, but he was a bit unlucky and hit the crossbar a few times. I've given him a break since the Irish Cesarewitch and he'll come back with a view to having a nice spring campaign over hurdles. He's better than we've seen on the track so far. 17-11-25

racecards.verdict: BLAKE is closely matched with Koktail Brut and Le Labo and if he jumps better he can reverse form with both those rivals
racecards.betting_forecast: 15/8 El Cairos, 4/1 Skylight Hustle, 11/2 Le Labo, 13/2 Koktail Brut, 8/1 Blake, 10/1 Sober, 12/1 Eachtotheirown, 20/1 Too Bossy For Us, 50/1 Free Spirit

racecards.race_name: Dooley Insurance Group Champion Novice Chase (Grade 1)

runners.comment: A revelation when winning 2m4f Grade 1 at Fairyhouse, fair chance of getting this trip
runners.spotlight: Won a 2m beginners' chase at Wexford in October; went close in a 2m Grade 2 here in November; after a break, well below his best at Thurles in March; career-best with the help of new hold-up tactics when outsider of eight in Grade 1 Fairyhouse, beating Kappa Jy Pyke; third in a Grade 1 novice hurdle here a year ago; fair chance of staying this far.

quotes.race: WillowWarm Gold Cup (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: This is my biggest day by a mile. I had a Group 2 winner on the Flat, but this definitely trumps that. We've sold a lot of Grade 1 horses through the years. We bought Fleur In The Park as a foal and he was second in a Grade 2 over hurdles, but we always thought he'd be a better chaser. He was unlucky to get beaten at Punchestown in a Grade 2 over fences earlier in the season and he got injured that day and was standing in a stable for a month. When he ran in Thurles he was only back on the go about six weeks and badly needed the run. We knew coming today that we had him as good as we could get him. I told the owners he wouldn't be out of the first three - Andrew Slattery, trainer.

quotes.race: racingtv.com Free Month Trial Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Fleur In The Park was only 80 per cent ready in Gowran. We knew he would improve. He could be a two-mile chaser because he jumps so well. Where we go next now, I'm not sure. Maybe we go travelling with him to somewhere with a lot of jumping, like Ascot. I didn't want to tempt fate and make a plan before today. We always thought he would be better over fences and hopefully he is - Andrew Slattery, trainer.

runners.comment: Failed to cope with Fleur In The Park at Fairyhouse, helps to add depth to stable's squad
runners.spotlight: Found wanting at Grade 1 level over hurdles last season; much more accomplished as a chaser; beat a long odds-on stablemate in Thurles beginners' event; beat Jacob's Ladder readily here in January in a Grade 3 race in which Predators Gold gave a below-par display; failed to cope with Fleur In The Park at Fairyhouse.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Super Sub Novice Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: We thought Kappa Jy Pyke was a decent horse last year and he ran well in his first maiden hurdle and then won. He was a bit disappointing afterwards for no reason. I'd say he's probably just strengthened up, and he jumped great. He jumped really quick early, and you'd be wondering about coming back in trip as he was jumping so fast. Danny [Mullins] said he relaxed when he pulled him out, and he put it to bed nicely. Paul [Townend] thought they went nice and even all the way. We thought he was a stayer last year. Two-and-a-half seems to be working at the moment, so we'll see what's around for him - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Thurles Racecourse Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Being the horse that Salvator Mundi is, you'd be thinking he would be hard to beat but, as the race developed, Kappa Jy Pyke's jumping was great and I was able to play it tactically late on. Thankfully, it came off. Willie wants us all going out to try and win, and thankfully I came out on top today - Danny Mullins, jockey.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Acca Freeze Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: It was a nice performance. Kappa Jy Pyke built on Cork well in every sense, jumping-wise and the freshness was gone out of him with the benefit of that run. I thought he quickened up smartly down the straight. I was actually quite taken with him - Paul Townend, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: I know the owners would love to go and they're from Cheshire. I'm thinking of looking at the WillowWarm Gold Cup at Fairyhouse, that looks to me an obvious target. However, the novice races could cut up at Cheltenham, so we'll see with him. 12-02-26

prev_owners.owner: Mme M Juhen-Cypres, D S De Beauregard & Mme T De Beauregard

runners.comment: Best of the Mullins quartet judged on his Brown Advisory win atoning for Sandown failure
runners.spotlight: Set the early standard in the staying novice division, winning Grade 1 Kauto Star at Kempton (3m, good) at Christmas after a 2m3f beginners' win at this venue; blotted his record in Sandown Grade 1, jumped right before unseating at the sixth; redeemed himself with a stylish front-running victory in the Brown Advisory; now looks strongest of the Mullins quartet.

quotes.race: Brown Advisory Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (Registered As The Broadway Novices' Chase) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was a hell of a performance. To make all in a Brown Advisory and then fight off what is a top horse in Final Demand - I thought Final Demand would have had his measure coming up the hill - what a brave performance. Things didn't go right for him Kitzbuhel the last day, but certainly he bounced back to form today - Willie Mullins, trainer.Kitzbuhel is braver than I am, this little chap. He's a phenomenal horse and was brilliant today, he was very brave. He was lugging right the whole way and that was why I just kept him down the middle. I had to switch in down the hill, as I wanted to make them come round me. He was so brave - everywhere I asked him, he delivered. Credit to the horse, he is very, very tough - Harry Cobden, jockey.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Kauto Star Novices' Chase (In Memory Of Nigel Clark) (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was wondering if the ground was too good for Kitzbuhel, but he handled it very well and he jumped off it fantastically. He gallops and stays, and what more can you want in a race horse. Looking at that, you'd think he could easily go back to two and a half miles, but nothing is written in stone yet. You're hoping that when you're jumping like that you don't make one mistake and let the whole field back into the race. We've a nice team of novice chasers, so hopefully they just stay sound. It's far too early for me to be planning anything with him, but we might look at the Dublin Racing Festival. We'll see how everything goes over Christmas before we make any plans - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Conway Piling Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Kitzbuhel needed that. It was a nice performance, he jumped economically and Paul [Townend] was happy that he'd improve from that. We'll look for a race after Christmas, maybe the one at Limerick - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Red Mills Trial Hurdle (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: I love the way Kitzbuhel jumped, he'd have no trouble going over fences. I loved the way he stayed on when it looked like the race was over when he was taken on by Sir Gerhard and he had to find again to take on the challenge of Break My Soul. It's the sign of a real good horse that he was able to pick up a second time. I'm probably looking at Liverpool more so than Cheltenham. With the timing of the race and the two and a half miles for the Liverpool Hurdle, Aintree would be a big possibility. I think he'd love to step up in trip and I'd have no problem going three miles - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Members Club 2025 Hurdle
quotes.quote: He was very professional. I think Kitzbuhel will stay further, he surprised me the way he quickened into the straight - Paul Townend, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He did well over hurdles last season, but I'd like to think there's more to come from him over fences. He's a fine stamp of a horse who should really take to chasing. He wants a trip. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Non-runner
runners.spotlight: Non-runner

quotes.race: Cavan Developments Supporting Kill GAA Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Lovely Hurling seems to be improving and is one to look forward to. I'm not sure what the plan is, he looks like one who can step up in grade. He has only run on soft ground so I don't know how he will handle better ground, but he has plenty of size and scope. He would get you out of bed in the morning - Colm Murphy, trainer

runners.comment: Fine effort when winning a three-runner Cork event, takes a big jump in class.
runners.spotlight: Point, bumper and maiden hurdle winner; off the mark over fences at this track (2m5f) in November; better effort when second to C'Est Ta Chance in a Thurles novice event over a similar trip; good effort when winning a three-runner Cork event; takes a big jump in class.

quotes.race: BAR 1 Betting Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: It looked like it was all going so well but you just don't know.  Nowwhatdoyouthink is a lovely horse. We've been in front before and got nabbed so we were just trying to follow away. He's so big that he's able to nearly hurdle fences. The one big worry we had was that Willie's wouldn't make it and then we'd have to go and make it. But he's growing up, maybe he'd be able to do it now but it was nice to be able to follow. The other horse has been there and done it and we hoped we were on an upward swing. This is my biggest win, it's kind of hard to believe it. He's the best horse we've had now. We weren't able to sell him and thank god we weren't. I'd say the novice chase over 3m at Punchestown is next. We'll have to give him a crack at it. Liam [Quinlan] is local. He comes in and helps me out every morning. He's an unbelievable horseman. He's gifted -  Ray Hackett, trainer

quotes.race: William Hill Each Way Extra Challenge Series Irish EBF Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: That's a bit more like what Nowwhatdoyouthink is capable of. He gave him a great ride. He held onto him great and didn't really go for him. He has a big engine and it's just getting it all out of him. We'll take today and see what he does after that. I was thinking of a handicap in Limerick before the race, but we might look at something else now - Ray Hackett, trainer.

quotes.race: ThurlesRaces.ie Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: He has sound point-to-point form and Nowwhatdoyouthink's Cork bumper win is working out well. He got a bang in Listowel so you would forgive him that but we couldn't believe how bad he was at Punchestown and we found he had an issue with his wind so we got that tidied up and that was obviously a big help today. You see how lairy he was at the finish. Hopefully better races, where he'd be running at horses would suit. We were dreaming big at one stage but we're starting small again here and working our way back up - Ray Hackett, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Woodlands House Hotel Adare (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: Nowwhatdoyouthink is still a big baby and if he had a lead for longer it would have been better. It wouldn't make sense to jump hurdles now so he'll either go to Punchestown for a winners' bumper or go out to grass - Ray Hackett, trainer

runners.comment: Late progress to finish fourth behind Kitzbuhel at Cheltenham, unseated in Grand National
runners.spotlight: Prospered after second to Western Fold on chase debut at Tipperary last May; hat-trick included small-field 3m Grade 2s at this venue and Navan; took time to warm up and left with plenty to do in the Brown Advisory, made late progress to finish fourth behind Kitzbuhel; towards the back when unseated at the 15th (Chair) in the Grand National.

quotes.race: William Hill Racing Bet Builder Ten Up Novice Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: I wasn't going overly quick because of the testing ground. Oscars Brother jumped really well and hit the line well. He's versatile ground-wise although I do think the slower the ground the better, 3m is the key- Daniel King, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.  After the last day, we had this race pencilled in and I suppose we can make more plans now. Oscars Brother takes his racing well, so we will see how he is during the week and go from there. The timing of the Brown Advisory would be good. He keeps improving, so you never know where he could end up. We did the National entry last week and while we would need one more run to qualify, we still have time on our side - Connor King, trainer

quotes.race: Boodles Florida Pearl Novice Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: We've always liked Oscars Brother. He did well over hurdles, but we always hoped he'd be a better chaser. I've been keeping my eye on this race for a long time. I remember watching this race last year just before I rode him out and I thought it'd be a nice race to aim for. It's disappointing for us that they have got rid of the three-mile novice chase at Leopardstown as that would have been ideal. Limerick [the Faugheen Novice Chase] is two mile five and it will probably be heavy ground so that might suit him, and we could travel as well - Connor King, trainer.He's a dream to ride and to train. Oscars Brother was good and tough today, he's improving away. He's such a good attitude, jumps for fun so a nice horse to look forward with - Daniel King, jockey.

runners.comment: Going well when falling two out in the 2m4f Fairyhouse Grade 1 won by Fleur In The Park
runners.spotlight: Smart novice hurdler in 2023-24 season before 19-month absence; returned to win a beginners' event at Navan in December, beating Slade Steel; jumping was untidy when he was beaten at odds-on by stablemate Kappa Jy Pyke here in January; challenging and going well when falling two out in the 2m4f Fairyhouse Grade 1 won by Fleur In The Park.

quotes.race: Watch Danny's Diary @ToteRacing Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: This is a Willie Mullins masterpiece. Predators Gold was nearly a year and a half off the track and then comes back to win a race like that, beating Slade Steel and Wingmen. It's some training performance - Danny Mullins, jockey.

quotes.race: CourtClinic.ie Chartered Physiotherapists Supporting Kilmacud Crokes GAA Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Predators Gold was fresh but he put it to bed fairly quickly. He put in a massive jump at the last and he had plenty left in the tank - Paul Townend, rider.

stable_tour.quote: I imagine he'll go to the Baring Bingham. He was too keen at Leopardstown and may just need different headgear to settle him, but they'll be going at a much faster pace in that race which will suit him well. 13-02-24

runners.breeder: E A R L Elevage Des Loges
runners.comment: Kerry National winner last autumn, non-finisher four times since then, very risky
runners.spotlight: Smart staying handicapper at his best; won the Kerry National at Listowel last September and looked set for victory in the Thyestes at Gowran Park in January when unseating at the final fence; pulled up in the Bobbyjo at Fairyhouse, same outcome in the Grand National.

quotes.race: Guinness Kerry National Handicap Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Spanish Harlem wasn't the cheapest horse but he just hasn't been firing. We put cheekpieces on him and he got his jumping right at long last. Danny [Mullins, jockey] came up with a plan which was to jump out, give him plenty of daylight and it worked. He jumped super but made one or two mistakes. He'll iron that out too. We'd love to produce him for the Randox Grand National at Aintree. I suppose we'd have to have a go at the Munster National or the Coral Gold Cup at Newbury and raise it like that. I think he likes nicer ground, that could be the key to him as well as plenty of jumping and longer trips - Willie Mullins, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Jim Ryan Memorial Novice Chase
quotes.quote: Sean [Cleary-Farrell] gave Spanish Harlem a good ride and he kept galloping well. I'd say nicer ground suits him and obviously those extended trips. He ran a real good race at Sandown. I'd say he'll be looking at races like the Kerry National and Munster National - David Casey, trainer's assistant.

stable_tour.quote: Cheekpieces have really helped him and brought him on. He jumped really well when winning the Kerry National and hopefully he could turn into a Grand National horse this season. He's another of mine who holds an entry in the Coral Gold Cup at Newbury. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Needs to recapture early-season form, Galway Plate winner and Grade 2 Gowran scorer
runners.spotlight: Progressive in the first half of the season; won the Galway Plate, beat subsequent Savills Chase winner Affordale Fury at Gowran in October; second to Kaid d'Authie in an unsatisfactory four-runner DRF event; faded from three out in Brown Advisory; badly hampered and unseated two out in Fairyhouse Grade 1 won by Fleur In The Park.

quotes.race: PWC Champion Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Western Fold could head to Down Royal for the Champion Chase or we could keep him for the Drinmore. He didn't win over fences until Tipperary in May so he's a novice for the whole year. I don't know if there are many novices with the experience he has. Danny [Gilligan, jockey] gets a good tune out of him. I was going to put Jack [Kennedy] on him but come Down Royal and the Drinmore, Jack will have other horses to ride so I said I'd keep the combination together - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Tote Galway Plate (Handicap Chase) (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Everything worked out great. Danny got away at the start and Western Fold jumped like a buck, I think he just missed one into the Dip. Everything went right and it was poetry in motion. I thought the 10lb rise might be enough to stop him to be honest. I'd say the ground is the key to this horse, he likes a bit of nice ground - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Franciscan Well Rated Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: Western Fold was keen with me two runs back and I rode him to get settled today. He did it well and will get further - Jack Kennedy, rider

stable_tour.quote: I couldn't believe how well he ran at the Dublin Racing Festival as he hadn't been back doing full work for long. He'll come on loads for that and that makes me think he has a big chance in the Brown Advisory. The ground should suit and he's got lots of experience, which will stand him in good stead in a race like that.  09-02-26

prev_owners.owner: C B Woods & Mr N Doolin

runners.comment: Only mare in the field, reservations about stamina and seems short of the standard needed
runners.spotlight: Won Grade 2 Arkle Trial over 2m at Cheltenham in November before finishing third in 2m1f event at Leopardstown in December; appeared not to stay the extended 2m4f in the Grade 2 mares' chase at the Cheltenham Festival; however, she was placed in a Grade 1 hurdle around this distance in France two seasons ago.

quotes.race: Paddy Power Arkle Challenge Trophy Trial Novices' Chase (Grade 2) (Registered As The November) (GBB)
quotes.quote: July Flower is very exciting. She was very good at Limerick the other day and we said we'd drop back in trip and see. We are delighted with her - she jumped great. I delighted for the Angoves [owners] and Darragh [O'Keeffe, jockey]. We were in two minds about going over fences in the summer, but Duncan [Angove] was happy to go and thankfully we did. We'll take it one step at a time - Henry de Bromhead, trainer.

quotes.race: Beat The Bank.ie Irish EBF Mares Hurdle (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: July Flower can be keen but she settled lovely today. The race panned out ideally for her and she picked up again in the straight. Her jumping is exceptional; that's a big asset to her. She's got some really good form in France and it was great to see her reproduce that over here - Rachel Blackmore, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: She's adaptable and her form's pretty good over any trip. I thought she improved for the drop in trip when she won at Cheltenham in November, then she ran a little disappointingly at Leopardstown over Christmas. It might have been that the ground and trip [2m1f on yielding] just put her out a little. She was winging fences and I thought she was going to win turning in, but she seemed to tire before the last. She's in the Mares' Chase and the Arkle, and I'm leaning towards the Mares'. It would make sense, looking at the way the Arkle is shaping up, but we'll see. 15-02-26

runners.comment: E200,000 3yo, half-brother to the talented Santini, noteworthy with Derek O'Connor booked
runners.spotlight: E65,000 2yo, E200,000 3yo; tenth foal; half-brother by Nathaniel to winners, notably the talented Santini; dam 1m4f Flat/2m hurdle winner; could be a big player with Derek O'Connor aboard.

runners.comment: E60,000 3yo, dam Limini was talented and versatile, strong trainer/rider combination
runners.spotlight: E75,000 foal, E60,000 3yo; Nathaniel gelding second foal out of Limini, a middle distance Flat winner and smart hurdle winner for Willie Mullins; family of Irish Oaks winner Vintage Tipple; strong trainer/rider combination.

runners.comment: E52,000, should be better for a maiden hurdle outing at Clonmel, trainer has a strong hand
runners.spotlight: E52,000; fifth foal, Westerner gelding is a brother to very useful hurdle/chase winner Amarillo Sky; should be better for a maiden hurdle outing at Clonmel; trainer has a strong hand.

runners.comment: E38,000 3yo (vendor), disappointing favourite on debut over C&D; rejected by Harry Swan
runners.spotlight: E45,000 foal, (E38,000 vendor 3yo); seventh foal; half-brother to hurdle/chase winner Mr Incredible; disappointing favourite on debut over C&D; rejected by Harry Swan now.

runners.comment: E160,000 3yo, probably unsuited by modest gallop when second to a Mullins runner on debut
runners.spotlight: E160,000 3yo; fourth foal; half-brother by Walk In The Park to recent debut bumper winner Emerald Enigma; dam is closely related to winners, notably the talented Identity Thief; probably unsuited by modest gallop when no match for a Willie Mullins-trained odds-on chance at Gowran in January; heads a five-runner squad for Gordon Elliot.

runners.spotlight: E52,000 3yo; half-brother to two French winners; finished with only one behind him at Leopardstown first time out.

runners.comment: E20,000 3yo (vendor), failed to sell, good pedigree boosted lately by half-sister Zanoosh
runners.spotlight: E20,000 3yo (vendor); 12th foal; half-brother by Order Of St George to six winners, including recent Grade 1 hurdles winner Zanoosh, Listed Flat scorer Paiardina, Brave Eagle (nine races over jumps), Nucky Johnson (bumper/ hurdle); dam 1m4f winner.

runners.comment: E72,000 3yo; dam won on the Flat and has a decent record at stud,  respected connections
runners.spotlight: E38,000 F, E72,000 3yo; ninth foal; Telescope gedling, brother to point/bumper/hurdle winner Seeyouinmydreams, half-brother to three winners including Songe (Flat/hurdle/chase) and Sandy Cay (Flat/hurdle); dam won on Flat; respected connections.

runners.comment: Half-brother to two German winners, stable's Bacharach was a much more expensive purchase
runners.spotlight: E11,000 Y, E24,000 3yo; fourth foal; half-brother to two German winners; dam German Group 3 winner; stable's Bacharach was a much more expensive purchase.

runners.spotlight: E145,000 3yo; second foal; dam French 2m1f hurdle winner; one of two fillies in the race for the champion trainer who has won three of the last five editions; rider and owners bidding for a repeat of shared 2023 success; likely to be in the mix.

runners.comment: E30,000 3yo, third foal; dam a bumper/chase winner by Kings Theatre; cheekpieces fitted
runners.spotlight: E23,000 F, E30,000 3yo; third foal; filly by Crystal Ocean out of a bumper/chase winner by Kings Theatre; cheekpieces fitted.

runners.comment: E15,000 3yo, cheap purchase, pedigree boosted by her dam's sister The Mourne Rambler
runners.spotlight: E15,000 3yo; first foal; Jet Away filly out of an unraced sister to stable's Champion Bumper winner The Mourne Rambler, and two other useful performers, Sixshooter and She's A Star.

runners.breeder: Scea Des Prairies,Snc Ecurie De Castillon,Sas Haras De Bourg

runners.spotlight: E23,000 Y, E42,000 3yo; fifth foal; half-sister to two Flat/hurdle winners; dam 1m4f winner by Authorized, half-sister to a 1m Listed winner; trainer saddled the third in this last year.

runners.comment: E15,500 3yo; second in a maiden hurdle at Clonmel, that experience should be an asset
runners.spotlight: E15,500 3yo; sixth foal; half-sister by Yeats to winners, notably Lowry's Bar (six races); made a satisfactory debut when second in a maiden hurdle at Clonmel; experience should be an asset, but this is a different sort of test.

runners.comment: E88,000 3yo; third foal; half-sister to French hurdle/chase winner La Delirante
runners.spotlight: E88,000 3yo; third foal; half-sister to French hurdle/chase winner La Delirante; dam unraced sister to French 2m4f Grade 3 chase winner Royale Francois.
