racecards.race_name: William Hill Champion Chase (Grade 1)

prev_owners.owner: Ecurie Herve Guerin, Gabriel Leenders Et Al

runners.comment: Fourth chase win in Naas Gr'3 on penultimate, 6l behind Energumene on latest
runners.spotlight: One of four for Willie Mullins; gained a fourth chase win in a Naas Grade 3 in February; creditable effort when a 6l runner up behind Energumene in a Fairyhouse Grade 2 on latest; 3lb worse off with that rival here and looks set to play a supporting role again.

quotes.race: William Hill Racing Bet Builder Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: It's great to win. Blood Destiny wasn't giving lumps of weight away like he was the last day and he obviously likes it around here. He won a good novice race around here. He was on a going day and he did it well. He has disappointed a lot of times. He's had a couple of issues but on his day he's not a bad horse and today thankfully was a going day. We'll see what else is around for him. The conditions of the race suited him today - David Casey, trainer.

quotes.race: John J. Galvin Chase
quotes.quote: Blood Destiny enjoyed it and winning that will do him the world of good. He did what he was expected to do there. I don't know if they are going to keep going with him now and farm those races hopefully or leave him off. This lad is not old and I would say he will have other career options, not just farm these races. He was a good juvenile but he is just hard to win with. He likes nice ground, he is better on nicer ground than heavy winter ground but he is adaptable. The way he jumps you could drop him back to two miles, he was keen with me early on so you could bring him back in trip as well - Paul Townend, jockey.

quotes.race: Flyingbolt Novice Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: We tried new tactics and I thought that might be a help after Punchestown. Paul [Townend] was very taken with Blood Destiny there. He's brilliant to jump, that was always his feature, but we were making too much use of his jumping instead of just using it when we needed it. Coming back in trip might have been a help as well. I don't know whether we've made a mistake now leaving him at home for Cheltenham but at least he has one nice prize in the bag. I imagine he'll probably go for the WillowWarm Gold Cup at Fairyhouse. That was the plan, here and then on to that - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Bar One Racing "Bet 10 Euro Get 50 Euro Sign Up Offer" Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Blood Destiny was dynamite everywhere and always looking for the next fence really. He's a real chaser. They tried to push me and get him lit up, but I wasn't interfering with him and he was getting a length everywhere with his jumping - Paul Townend, rider

quotes.race: Race Displays Hurdle
quotes.quote: Blood Destiny has obviously improved again from his win at Cork and just has a lovely way of going about it. He was idle enough and missed a couple of hurdles but he was doing nothing - Paul Townend, rider.

quotes.race: Bar One Racing 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Paul (Townend, rider) had lots of confidence in Blood Destiny, and when he let him stride on he jumped those hurdles well. The experience he got in France helped. He does that nicely in the juvenile division and will make a chaser in time. Hopefully he will go forward. Whether it's too close for him to run at Christmas or not, we'll see. We might wait but will see how he comes out of this. I hope he comes home safe and sound and I'll be planning a Grade 1 route with him - Willie Mullins, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's just back in training following a little break after his run at Gowran. We'll find something suitable when he's ready to start back. 17-11-25

He's a very interesting prospect for the Triumph Hurdle having won his two races for us very impressively, particularly last time at Fairyhouse. We didn't run him at the Dublin Racing Festival as it was only three weeks after his previous run and that would have been a big ask for a youngster. Having missed that race, he'll be going over next week a much fresher horse. I think he's very good. 08-03-23

runners.comment: Rolled back the years on latest, won this in 2022 & 2023, vulnerable to younger legs
runners.spotlight: Rolled back the years with a dominant win at Fairyhouse on latest, his first start at 2m4f for almost six years; won this in 2022 and 2023 but he's a 12yo now and Paul Townend prefers the chances of Il Etait Temps; probably vulnerable to younger legs dropped back in trip.

quotes.race: Underwriting Exchange Fairyhouse Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: I couldn't believe how well Energumene was going as you could just see Paul [Townend] absolutely tanking. I'm delighted with Blood Destiny too, but feel very sorry for Saint Sam [fatal injury at second-last] and connections. At 12 years of age, to put in a performance like that. He ran like a seven or eight-year-old, it's tremendous. I think he'll have an entry at Punchestown and I'll have a chat with connections to see what they feel - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: BetMGM Clarence House Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: "On that ground, Jonbon had too much speed for Energumene. The race didn't pan out to suit us. Paul [Townend, jockey] just said he got alongside Jonbon at the fourth last and he just picked up and went away from him. Jonbon is a nine-year-old and reaching his peak, whereas our fella is 11. We just need to pick our battles and have the right conditions, and that would mean very soft ground. If the ground came up heavy at Cheltenham like it did last year, you'd maybe have a pop - Sean Graham, owner's racing manager.

quotes.race: Bar One Racing Hilly Way Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: The Clarence House Chase was what we did previously, so we'll see how Energumene comes out of it before making any decision - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Champion Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Energumene gave a couple of fences fair belts, which is uncharacteristic for him really. I think it showed how good a horse he is to do things not perfectly today and win, because we know how good Chacun Pour Soi can be on home soil - Paul Townend, rider.

quotes.race: Betway Queen Mother Champion Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Energumene was just brilliant on the day and Paul was just brilliant on him. I was way more confident coming into this year's race as we hadn't got Shishkin to take on and we thought if there was any improvement from the Clarence House that hopefully with a clear round he would win. Paul came home from the Clarence House and said they won't beat us again. The whole game plan will be to work back from this next year - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Albert Bartlett Clarence House Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Up to the second last we were running a really good race. The winner (Editeur Du Gite) won on merit and I loved the way that he won after being passed and it was a great performance from the second (Edwardstone) too. Hopefully that run will get Energumene used to the new English white fences, we've schooled over them at home but he didn't seem as happy over them today as he did last March. You saw what he did at the first and he was a little bit long at one or two. It's different and I didn't expect him to be that way as he'd done plenty of schooling but he obviously did. I think the winner set the pace and won, it was a great performance and I'm not going to take anything away from him. We weren't able to beat him on the day. We just hope that there's a different result on the next day for us - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Champion Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Energumene is by the same sire as Un De Sceaux and looked like he might be a similar sort but he has a lot more speed than we gave him credit for. The fact that he was able to come off a pace like that shows it. He was still able to gallop away from them and show speed going down to the last fence. It tells me that he's improving all the time - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Betway Queen Mother Champion Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We just felt that we had completely the wrong tactics at Ascot. But today it wasn't about tactics so much - Shishkin just didn't handle that ground and Nico wisely pulled him up, and I was just very disappointed to see Chacun Pour Soi going out of the race early, but I could see Paul travelling and Energumene loving conditions here. It probably suited him better. He's got more speed than maybe we thought - at Ascot we thought after the race we should have waited, rather than play our cards early - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: SBK Clarence House Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Energumene ran his heart out and Paul gave him a terrific ride. Nico de Boinville was excellent on Shishkin and, of course, Shishkin did what he always does. He pretends to be beaten and then he nabs you on the line - although, to be fair, he usually does it a bit earlier than that. I think our fellow probably jumped a bit better than the winner. Shishkin might have that up his sleeve if he puts it all together next time. It's going to be difficult for us. I hope we're not going to be far away from him at Cheltenham but it's going to be difficult to turn it around. If I was looking at it as a neutral I would say Shishkin just has the edge. God knows what he had left in the locker as well. It's all to play for the next day but I would say the betting people will have Shishkin as favourite again - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Kerry Group Hilly Way Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: You would have to be delighted with that. Sean said they went very quick early, they ended up racing all the way down the back but Energumene's class told and he won very easily. But for that he would have been very impressive. But Notebook took him on and he finished last having had a run. Sean was very impressed and he will improve loads. At the moment there is no need to go further with him but we know he does stay - David Casey, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Ryanair Novice Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Energumene met a few wrong down the back but once he got his eye in again he was brilliant over the last four. A great performance to finish up the season. I thought he would be a two-and-a-half mile horse but when he gets his jumping right, he's like a hurdler jumping fences. He will go the Champion Chase route at first next season and see how that goes - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Patrick Ward & Company Solicitors Irish Arkle Novice Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Energumene put up a hell of a performance there to jump and gallop the way her did. He stood a little far off a couple of them but you couldn't ask more from a novice having just his third run over fences - Willie Mullins, trainer

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Novice Chase
quotes.quote: Energumene was very impressive and he has a great method of jumping. He's obviously not too bad over this trip. That was very testing ground to do most of his own work. We'll probably go down the 2m route now and the Irish Arkle would look to be the next target - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: He loves chasing and Paul was very taken with him which has to be a good sign. We'll probably find something for him around Christmas. Paul said he wouldn't mind going back in trip but he could easily go up in trip as he has a nice relaxed way of galloping - Willie Mullins, trainer

quotes.race: MansionBet Get Paid As A Winner If 2nd In The Supreme Novices' At Cheltenham Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Energumene jumped fantastic when he was going at racing speed. I would like to get a couple of runs into him before Punchestown and go for a novice hurdle there. He'll go chasing next year, that will be his forte - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Holy Cross Flat Race
quotes.quote: I'd say he's still learning and will learn from today. His future will lie over fences. I'm not sure what the plan is with him, plenty of horses missed last year with the ground and he was around then. I'd say he has a fair engine - David Casey, assistant trainer to Willie Mullins, trainer of Energumene\P

stable_tour.quote: Now might be the time to try him over a bit further than two miles. I know he's an 11-year-old, but he seems in great shape at home and we're looking forward to getting him out. He's entered in the John Durkan. 17-11-25

He won me a first Champion Chase last year and followed up at Punchestown the following month. This season he started off with an easy win at Cork in the Hilly Way. I then took him over for the Clarence House, which had been rerouted from Ascot to Cheltenham, and he finished third. I think he needed the run over those different style of fences. Even though we had schooled him over them at home, sometimes a horse just needs to get out on the course and see them while racing. I feel that experience will stand to him at the festival. There's never a slowly run Champion Chase and I think that'll suit our fellow. The Clarence House was a very tactical race and some of the jockeys might change tactics next time. We learned a lot and Paul [Townend] is happy he'll improve a good deal from that experience. 08-03-23

runners.breeder: E Clayeux & S C Ecurie Couderc
runners.comment: 8-11 over fences including six Grade 1s, bolted up in Champion Chase latest, big chance
runners.spotlight: Ground versatile; not the biggest in stature but a hugely talented performer who has won eight of his 11 chase starts, including six Grade 1s; bolted up in the Champion Chase on latest, immediately bouncing back from a rare blip at Sandown; won a Grade 1 novice over C&D at this meeting last year and he's preferred by Townend; leading chance.

quotes.race: BetMGM Queen Mother Champion Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought Paul [Townend] was very brave on Il Etait Temps because he couldn't go the pace they were setting for the first mile; he sat and sat, and coming down the hill we could all see that the further he was going, the better he was going. I nearly had a heart attack at the last fence though! But the horse has come to himself at last. Taking the hood off and this ground made a big difference to him as well, I'd say. That was way his best performance at Cheltenham. I was wondering, was he a horse that didn't like this place? But when we went through his form here we found excuses for every run, and perhaps it wasn't so bad after all. We had to do something. Since the time he was a young horse he was always very keen. He's always worn a hood, and then after Ascot we knew we had to change something, and we think that made a real difference. It probably took him 24 hours to recover when he came home from Ascot. You have to remember, he was a bit shaken and then he has to get on the ferry, which isn't what you'd do really, but it was what we did, and once he got home he settled into his own routine and he recovered quite quickly. He was always going to run in this race, but we had to get the old spark back into him. I think Paul said it, he doesn't need the hood anymore, so that was number one, and a few little tweaks at home after that, and we just galloped him a bit differently, a bit like Lossiemouth, and it's worked. And I think the early pace here today, even though he couldn't go that pace it suited him, and Paul - having someone like Paul who didn't panic and try to keep up; he knew that they were going too fast and they might come back to him - Willie Mullins, trainer.I got a good start and I jumped the first couple OK, but I was always just going to go my speed, and it wasn't as fast as they were going up front! But I wasn't going to put Il Etait Temps on his head - the best way to get him back wasn't going to be to force him and go too fast. But that's thing about riding for the likes of Willie - they know why you're doing it, and it all came good in the end. I thought taking the hood off would help. It's hard to change it when he's winning, but if you're knocked back, you can change it up then. He's so tough, he's so mentally tough to come back after Ascot. A lot of work went into him after that and there are a lot of people to thank - I'm lucky enough to get to hand him back at the end of the day and arrive on him next time knowing he's in tip-top condition. I thought it was brilliant that Majborough was going off in front and favourite - there was no pressure on me. He was the silent horse coming into the race, and a lot of people had written him off after one bad run. For a change, the pressure was on someone else! At turn of the top of the hill, I'd seen Mark [Walsh, rider of Majborough] making me a mistake. My lad was gaining in confidence all the time and they weren't going to get any further away from me - Paul Townend, j

quotes.race: Betfair Tingle Creek Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Il Etait Temps is tiny, isn't he? But he answered every question I asked of him today. I feel a bit silly for not picking him so many times in his career, but thankfully we're making up for it now. He's showing us all the promise he had as a young horse. He went through the race really easily. You can do what you want with him now, but in years gone by, you'd be afraid to ask him for a jump early in case it set him alight. He's so straightforward and tough now. He's measured and clean in his jumps, which is what you want any horse to do, whatever size. He's great - Paul Townend, jockey, speaking to ITV Racing.

quotes.race: Clonmel Oil Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: Il Etait Temps was very settled early, and for a long way I wondered if he was too settled. He took the lead before I wanted to. He woke up and settled it quickly. Down the hill, when he got competitive with the horse in front of him, he knew he was going back racing. Willie's plan before he left [for America and Australia] was the Tingle Creek. We always thought an awful lot of him, but he didn't jump hurdles well. He's only a handy horse but jumps fences economically and well. The engine was always there but he'd been hard on himself and it's taken him time to mature, and us time to figure him out - Paul Townend, jockey.

quotes.race: bet365 Celebration Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The instructions were for Danny [Mullins, jockey] to get as much place money as he could. Danny felt Il Etait Temps never jumped as well as today. He's had a little knee problem and every time we got to 90 per cent he had a setback but he's been working very well at home the last few weeks - Willie Mullins, trainer.You can't discount Willie Mullins horses after a layoff - he's a true champion. It was an impressive performance. His jumping was unbelievable. He put together a fantastic round. He looked around a bit coming to the last but he ran out an easy winner - Danny Mullins, jockey.

quotes.race: Barberstown Castle Novice Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Il Etait Temps is an extraordinary horse, that's his third Grade 1 this year.  He doesn't look like a big steeplechaser but he's got an engine and he jumps well. He's just maturing and learning all the time - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Close Brothers Manifesto Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was nice. I loved the manner in which Il Etait Temps did it. I was really taken with how he walked round the parade ring before the race - I haven't seen him as loose for a while, and I thought if he could run like he walked, he'd run a big race. And then when he jumped off at the start, I think for the first three-quarters of a circuit, I was very worried. He just seemed very behind himself, and I don't think he'll need his hood in future. But he warmed to his task, jumped well later in the race and he just kept galloping. Jukebox Jury is a right sire and we'll be using more of him. I think probably trip is more important than track to him. He did win over two miles, but this performance today over two and a half is fantastic. At this end of the season horses are tired and he took a bit of time to warm into it, but I'm happy that he's going to improve for further a trip as he gets older. He's a fine horse, probably only 16.1hh if that - the normal sort for today is a big 16.3hh chaser - and the important thing about him is that he turns up for everything. He's made of iron. There's never an issue with him, and that counts for a great deal - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Goffs Irish Arkle Novice Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Il Etait Temps is obviously very effective over this trip and we'll look forward to the Arkle in Cheltenham. He showed plenty of resolution and Danny just timed his run well - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Guinness Faugheen Novice Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: It was a great run. Il Etait Temps is proving himself as a Grade 1 novice chaser. He was very consistent in his novice hurdle season and he is showing he will be competitive in all of those Grade 1 novice chases. His jumping was good, although the winner's was something else - Danny Mullins, jockey.

quotes.race: Download The BetVictor App Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Il Etait Temps paid a lot more respect to his fences than he did hurdles. I thought he jumped brilliantly overall. It was a good gallop, a good horse led us and he showed a good turn of foot from the last - Paul Townend, rider

quotes.race: Tattersalls Ireland Novice Hurdle (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Il Etait Temps is a very good horse. He's just got to get his jumping right, he made a mistake at the first again today. He's a Grade 1 horse - Willie Mullins, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's in the Ryanair but I'd say him and Majborough will go to the Champion Chase. He was fine after his fall and is back riding out. There was no spark in him the last day. He surprised me last year with what he did at Sandown and he came back and repeated the dose in the Tingle Creek. 12-02-26

I always thought he was a fair horse, which is why we ran him in the races we did last year and he ended up being a novice for this season. He finished a four-length second to Facile Vega over Christmas but turned the tables on him last time at Leopardstown. He made a mistake at the first that day but Danny said that when he turned down the back he flew his hurdles and got it all together. I know the two ahead of him made it easier for him, but now it's all falling into place who knows how good he'll be? He's very keen but when he settles I think his jumping will come together. I know we have Facile Vega in the Supreme but this fellow will be a live one as well. 08-03-23

runners.comment: Three-time Grade 1 winner, erratic jumper at times, big chance if jumps well but risky
runners.spotlight: 4-8 over fences; has a massive engine and has won three Grade 1s over fences, including when giving Marine Nationale a 19l beating in first-time cheekpieces at the DRF; however, his jumping is often erratic and the cheekpieces weren't as effective when he again jumped poorly when soundly beaten in the Champion Chase; obvious chance if he jumps well but hard to know what to expect; a risky proposition.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Dublin Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: That's more like it. Mark [Walsh] wanted to do things his way and it paid off. The horse was a lot happier doing it, so it's onwards and upwards. Mark was adamant Majborough wanted cheekpieces on and he wanted to ride him his own way. All credit to him. It was poetry in motion down the back. I was afraid he might not have enough left in the tank over the second-last, but Mark said he had plenty - Willie Mullins, trainer.That's the real Majborough. At Cork, he can't go right-handed, he was too lairy in front and he wasn't jumping. Here the last day, I tried to hold him up in behind horses to get a lead but when I came in I said we were doing the wrong thing. He has such a big stride that it's his biggest asset, so Willie rang me the other morning and said we'd stick a set of cheekpieces on him and let him roll in front. It was the best thing that ever happened to him because it made a man of him today. When he is in front without the cheekpieces, he just doesn't concentrate, but he was looking at what he was doing today and sorting himself out. At the second fence he came up out of my hands but he cleared it - he has some power behind him - Mark Walsh, jockey.

quotes.race: Paddy's Rewards Club Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Majborough jumped better, the change of tactics was good, although maybe we need to tweak them more still - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: BAR 1 Betting Hilly Way Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: I was disappointed with Majborough's jumping. It didn't hold together going down the back and he paid the price for that. I was hoping he'd jump a lot better. But there you are, it's a bit disappointing, but hopefully he can improve for later in the season. I'm hoping that run will bring him on. He just needs to improve his jumping to be competitive at that level. We'll look at Christmas with him if he recovers well from this race - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Barberstown Castle Novice Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Majborough is huge but light framed and the moment he stepped off the lorry at home I thought he could be some article. Looking at Fact To File and then at him, there are similar attributes. He's only five and a summer's grass will help him come back bigger and stronger. I'd imagine you'd have to look at the Champion Chase possibly but he could go up in trip as he seems easy enough to ride. If he keeps jumping like that he could be scary - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: My Pension Expert Arkle Challenge Trophy Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was delighted with Majborough to finish third after the three mistakes he made. So we know he has a huge engine but we've got to get his jumping right. While I'm disappointed not to win, we're happy that we have a horse with an engine. I'm surprised that he did that but that's what can happen in the heat of battle here. He seems fine - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Goffs Irish Arkle Novice Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: That [jump at the third last] sort of put it to bed. I was surprised Mark [Walsh, jockey] was in the position he was jumping the second, third and fourth, but he was happy enough that Majborough wanted to be there. He's always been a standout to me. Mark said he gave him a squeeze coming up to the winning post and he had plenty in the tank, which is a fair thing to say after running at that pace over two miles and a furlong around here. All he was doing was putting in an extra stride to be very safe. Any time he met it right he was picking up lengths. We'll have to jump a bit better as we'd want to be winging every fence to match Sir Gino because he's a huge talent - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: Majborough was very good. He made a few little mistakes as a novice would, and he had to do it the hard way in front, but he fairly motored over the last two fences when Paul [Townend] came to him on Tullyhill, and was very slick at them. I couldn't be happier. Fences were always going to be the making of him and that was a great introduction," Walsh added. "He's not a slow horse and he has plenty of gears, but he'll stay too - Mark Walsh, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: JCB Triumph Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I'm surprised at his price, 6-1. I expected him to be favourite. Majborough was my pick of this race. All of mine have been improving over the season for the second run and I couldn't get him out over Christmas before the Dublin Racing Festival. We were worried about that but obviously he needed the run and Mark learned an awful lot about him. He came back in and said 'the next day I'm going to make all the running' and that was the plan today. He was fifth, sixth the whole way around but that's how strong the pace was, that he couldn't even make it when he wanted to. The two of those [Majborough and Kargese] I thought were going to be first and second but the fact Storm Heart finished fifth just shows how fast the early pace was. When Majborough came into the yard and they told me this is our Triumph Hurdle horse this year, I'm looking at him and thought, he's a Gold Cup horse, a three-mile chaser. Physically, that's what he looked like. That'll be a few years down the road, we'll let him go novice chasing first - Willie Mullins, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We've all had our opinions on how he should be ridden. Mark [Walsh] just said he'd rather do what he wanted to do at Leopardstown and it worked like a dream. That was fantastic and I'd imagine if Mark can repeat that performance, he's going to run a fantastic race at Cheltenham. 12-02-26

runners.comment: 2025 Champion Chaser, won this last year, fresh, gets his ground, big chance
runners.spotlight: The 2025 Champion Chaser arrives here a fresher horse than most after missing Cheltenham with a sore neck; returned to action at Leopardstown in December with a pleasing effort behind Solness after making an early mistake; no match for Majborough at the DRF on testing ground but he's a much better horse on a sounder surface; won this in fine style last year and could repeat the dose.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Dublin Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: To be fair to Marine Nationale he battled on to finish second. You can see what happened to the rest of them, they all pulled up. It'll hopefully be a different state of play at Cheltenham on nicer ground. He's never run on heavy before, but I thought he might get away with it. He just didn't seem to enjoy it at any stage of the race. I'm disappointed not to win but we gave it a go. He's not a hard horse to get fit, so I could have skipped today but I wanted to support the race. That's what we did and I think we'll see a different horse on spring ground - Barry Connell, owner and trainer.

quotes.race: Paddy's Rewards Club Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Other than winning we couldn't be more pleased. You'd have to think the mistake might have made the difference; Marine Nationale was facing the other way, when you see it it's incredible. Sean said he let fly at the fence. He's just so well and it's one of those things. He hasn't made a mistake like that before but he might have just been fresh on his first run of the season. We'll come back for the Dublin Racing Festival and hopefully there won't be a repeat of that - Barry Connell, owner.

quotes.race: William Hill Champion Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Marine Nationale is a horse of a lifetime. He seems like he's been around forever but that's only his 12th run, we've had him since he was a 4yo. He's improved since Cheltenham. Badsworth Boy was eight, nine and ten when he won three Champion Chases, the only horse to win three, so his plenty of time - Barry Connell, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: BetMGM Queen Mother Champion Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Marine Nationale started in Naas in a Grade 2, and progressed with two good runs at Leopardstown - he was coming all the time. If you go back and look at his career, three runs - won an ordinary maiden hurdle, then improved a stone to win the Royal Bond, improved another stone to win here. He loves this place and comes alive here. We were very confident coming today but understated, because I was too confident the last day and didn't want to do that again. He travels, he jumps - he's everything you want in a Champion Chaser - Barry Connell, owner-trainer.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Dublin Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: On a bit of better ground, with the hill at Cheltenham, Marine Nationale will be a better horse again. I thought I might get to Solness coming down to the last but the ground is probably just a bit softer than he would ideally like. He's run an absolute cracker - Sean Flanagan, jockey.

quotes.race: Barberstown Castle Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: The winner was very good. I was happy though with Marine Nationale, though. He didn't meet the first two right, but once he warmed to it I thought his jumping was good. He probably lacked a a bit of experience. Other than not winning the race I was very happy. The first two were well clear of the rest. We'll go to Leopardstown at Christmas and build for the Champion Chase after that. I don't see any reason why we shouldn't. We would like to have won but other than that he acquitted himself well - Barry Connell, trainer.

quotes.race: Paddy Power From The Horses Mouth Podcast Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: As you've seen there, Marine Nationale's jumping is nothing to be worried about. He was foot perfect. He winged everything, he got in tight to one down the back but he was very clever doing so and didn't touch a twig. I went a nice gallop in front, he was probably a bit keener today than he's ever been on his first run in a while. He was lit up a bit but it was very straightforward, he's just a class act. He's having a good blow, I imagine he'll come on plenty for it - Michael O'Sullivan, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Supreme Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Marine Nationale is unlike any other horse we've had before - they were mainly stayers, this is a quick horse, he's probably a Group 1 horse on the Flat, and we might get around to that at some stage. But today was his day. He's had five runs and won all five. His jockey is a superstar. I think we'll come back here for the Arkle next year. Those are my initial thoughts at this period in time - Barry Connell, trainer.

quotes.race: Bar One Racing Royal Bond Novice Hurdle (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Marine Nationale travelled away and jumped well, he was awkward at the last, and that was the first time he has ever been off the bridle. I didn't know what he would do off the bridle but he showed that he was tough. I thought the ground was gone for him. He'll improve again - Barry Connell, trainer.

quotes.race: Festival 2023 On Sale Now Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: I don't think Marine Nationale missed a beat in terms of his jumping and is having a good blow afterwards. He wasn't as impressive as he was in his bumpers, but did what he had to do. He could probably do with another run and may go for a Grade 3 in Navan (For Auction Novice Hurdle on November 13), with a view to going for the Royal Bond Novice Hurdle at Fairyhouse (on December 4) after that, if he's still on track - Barry Connell, trainer-owner

quotes.race: Jim Ryan Race Services (Pro/Am) Flat Race
quotes.quote: Marine Nationale did what I expected and probably hasn't done any more than he did at Punchestown. They were proper winter horses at Punchestown and this was a summer bumper, but it's nice to confirm that his debut wasn't a flash in the pan. He has a relaxed temperament, which is a big plus, and he looks a decent prospect. He was in Sam Curling's so has plenty jumping done - we bought him before Sam had planned to run him in a four-year-old point-to-point. We'll look for a maiden hurdle somewhere. In the back of my head is the Royal Bond, if we can get a maiden hurdle and maybe a Grade 3 beforehand. He'll go on soft ground but I'd say he mightn't be a winter-ground horse. If everything went to plan he could go to the Dublin Racing Festival, and if the dream was still alive then Cheltenham. You have to think that way until something beats him - Barry Connell, owner/trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's come out of the Dublin Racing Festival in excellent form. He's improving 10lb every time he runs over fences as he's effectively a novice. That was his fifth chase run, and the winner's 17th. He did the donkey work of chasing down Solness and I think he'll come on for it. He's a course-and-distance winner on the Old course over hurdles, and his temperament is bombproof. He's the best Irish challenger in the race, although whether we beat Jonbon is another matter. He's in great nick at home. 20-2-25

racecards.verdict: MARINE NATIONALE (nap) is fresh after missing Cheltenham, he gets his favoured ground and he is taken to defend his crown

runners.comment: E60,000 3yo, half-brother to nine-time winner Brentford Hope, of some interest
runners.spotlight: E60,000 3yo; seventh foal; half-brother to three winners, notably Brentford Hope, who has won three races on the Flat and six over hurdles; dam French 1m3f winner; of some interest.

runners.comment: 11th foal; half-brother to two jumps winners, others have stronger claims on pedigree
runners.spotlight: 11th foal; half-brother to jumps winners Another Emotion and Linodargent; dam French 2m3f hurdle winner; others have stronger claims on pedigree.

runners.comment: Mastered by Willie Mullins-trained second favourite when favourite on debut,  can improve
runners.spotlight: Half-brother to three winners; well supported first time out in a bumper at Navan last month; raced a bit keenly and was mastered by the Willie Mullins-trained second favourite; could make his presence felt with that run under his belt.

runners.comment: Plenty of speed in his Flat pedigree, has to be taken seriously despite stamina doubt
runners.spotlight: E85,000 yearling; second foal; half-brother by Galiway (sire of Vauban) to French AW sprint winner Parisian Leah; dam unraced sister to 5f Group 3 winner Dibajj, half-sister to winners Black Sea (1m2f Listed) and Galvez (1m2f); has to be taken seriously despite stamina doubt.

runners.comment: Dam placed over hurdles/sister to a 7f 2yo winner, not one of the more obvious contenders.
runners.spotlight: First foal; dam placed over hurdles, sister to 7f 2yo winner Randall's Alannah; not one of the more obvious contenders.

runners.comment: E45,000 3yo, fourth foal; half-brother by Maxios to winners Warm In Gorey  and Bay Empress
runners.spotlight: E45,000 3yo; fourth foal; half-brother by Maxios to winners Warm In Gorey (three races over hurdles) and Bay Empress (bumper); dam hurdle winner.

runners.comment: E235,000 3yo, 6 1/2l in front of Jerpoint Abbey at Naas, winner took sixth at Cheltenham
runners.spotlight: E235,000 3yo; Blue Bresil gelding is a half-brother to the very useful Handstands and two other winners; could manage only third when favourite on debut at Naas in January; had 6 1/2l to spare over fourth-placed Jerpoint Abbey; Coole Cafe has boosted the form of the race and the winner Quiryn finished sixth in the Grade 1 bumper at Cheltenham.

runners.comment: Going well when falling two out in a point, dam a well-related bumper/hurdles winner
runners.spotlight: E37,000 F, (E30,000 vendor 3yo); second foal; dam a well-related bumper/hurdle winner; was going well when falling two out in a four-runner point at Ballycahane; has joined Paul Nolan from a good source.

runners.comment: Good pedigree but was never in the hunt on debut at Kilbeggan last Friday
runners.spotlight: Half-brother to a bumper winner; unraced dam out of half-sister to Champion Hurdle winners Morley Street and Granville Again; never in the hunt on debut at Kilbeggan last Friday.

runners.comment: First foal; dam unraced half-sister to useful hurdle/chase winner Steely Addition
runners.spotlight: E7,000 F; first foal; dam unraced half-sister to smart 2m5f-3m2f hurdle/chase winner Steely Addition, out of unraced half-sister to bumper and 2m-3m hurdle/chase winner Titian Blonde, in good hands.

runners.comment: E165,000 3yo; ninth foal; half-brother to five winners including the talented Black Corton
runners.spotlight: E62,000 2yo, E165,000 3yo; ninth foal; half-brother to five winners including Black Corton (14 races) and Hugos New Horse (seven races); dam unplaced 1m4f AQPS Flat; Jody Townend aboard, with Patrick Mullins on Delamotte.

runners.comment: Made a good first impression over hurdles at Cork despite a few untidy jumps
runners.spotlight: Fourth foal; dam an unraced half-sister to two 2m4f winners; made a good first impression over hurdles at Cork despite a few untidy jumps, ran on for second behind a Gordon Elliott-trained runner who had won an academy hurdle.

runners.comment: Half-brother to two winners, dam unraced half-sister to Ferny Hollow
runners.spotlight: E17,000, E16,000 3yo; sixth foal; half-brother to winners Hills Of Glory (point/2m3f hurdle) and Three Kings (point); dam unraced half-sister to Champion Bumper and high-class 2m/2m1f hurdle/chase winner Ferny Hollow.

runners.comment: Belated debut for E52,000 foal purchase, dam has a good staying Flat pedigree
runners.spotlight: E52,000 foal; first foal; dam unplaced 1m1f-1m6f (RPR 51), closely related to winners Nearly Caught (1m7f Group 2) and Katie's Reign (7f 2yo), half-sister to winners Pale Mimosa (2m Group 2) and Suailce (useful 1m4f/2m).

runners.comment: E140,000 3yo, first foal; dam useful bumper/ hurdle/chase winner, notable jockey booking
runners.spotlight: E140,000 3yo; first foal; dam useful bumper/hurdle/chase winner, half-sister to winners Tombstone and Walking On A Dream; one of three for his trainer, one of two for the owners along with the once-raced Hartford; notable jockey booking.

runners.comment: Unraced dam closely related to Irish 1,000 Guineas/Yorkshire Oaks winner Pleascach
runners.spotlight: Seventh foal; unraced dam closely related to Irish 1,000 Guineas/Yorkshire Oaks winner Pleascach; interesting with Derek O'Connor taking the ride for Jim Bolger.

runners.comment: Ninth foal, half-sister to bumper and high-class hurdle/chase winner Dunvegan
runners.spotlight: E7,000 Y; ninth foal; half-sister to bumper and high-class hurdle/chase winner Dunvegan, winner of six races for this yard.

runners.comment: Unsuited by heavy on debut, needs to reverse form with Hartford, not out of the question
runners.spotlight: Justify filly was a USD275,000 yearling purchase; half-sister to US 6.5f AW/1m dirt winner Lady Lowery; dam unraced half-sister to US Grade 3 1m AW winner Speightster, out of unraced sister to BC Distaff winner Dance Smartly; not a typical recruit to jumping.

runners.comment: Half-sister to five winners, dam unraced half-sister to the brilliant Denman, interesting
runners.spotlight: E30,000 3yo; 11th foal; half-sister by Soldier Of Fortune to five winners, including the useful Regent's Stroll; dam unraced half-sister to Cheltenham Gold Cup winner Denman; one for the short list.

runners.comment: Half-sister to Flat/hurdles winner Spanish John, dam 1m1f Flat winner
runners.spotlight: Fourth foal; half-sister to Flat/hurdle winner Spanish John; dam 1m1f Flat winner/maiden hurdler.

racecards.verdict: Probably unsuited by a modest gallop at Gowran in January, HARTFORD may be seen to better effect now in a true-run race
